The Experience

We are looking for a Cloud & DevOps Engineer, Senior Member of Technical Staff (SMTS), to design, build, automate, and operate reliable, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure and production platforms. You will work with software engineers, infrastructure teams, security partners, and product teams. Your work will improve service availability, deployment reliability, operational efficiency, and developer productivity.

The ideal candidate has strong experience with public cloud and cloud-native technologies, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, observability, and production operations. They also have practical software development experience in Python, Java, Go, or another programming language. This is an engineering-focused DevOps role. We expect automation and software development to replace repetitive manual operations.

You approach ambiguous infrastructure and production problems methodically. You understand system behavior across application and infrastructure layers. You use modern engineering practices, including AI-assisted development, to improve reliability, automation, and delivery effectiveness.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Design, build, automate, and operate secure, reliable, and scalable cloud infrastructure and production platforms.
  • Independently deliver well-scoped cloud, DevOps, reliability, and automation improvements after alignment on the overall technical plan and architecture.
  • Develop software, automation frameworks, scripts, APIs, and engineering tools in Python, Go, Java, or comparable languages. These reduce manual operations and improve platform reliability.
  • Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code for repeatable provisioning, configuration, deployment, and lifecycle management of cloud resources.
  • Develop and improve CI/CD pipelines that automate build, testing, security validation, deployment, rollback, and release processes.
  • Deploy and operate containerized workloads using Kubernetes or comparable cloud-native platforms.
  • Apply cloud and distributed-systems concepts such as scalability, fault tolerance, service communication, networking, availability, resiliency, and capacity management.
  • Build and improve observability using metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerts, and health checks. These give the team actionable visibility into production systems.
  • Diagnose production incidents using telemetry and system-level analysis. Identify contributing factors and root causes, and implement improvements that prevent recurrence.
  • Identify repetitive operational activities and convert them into safe, testable, and maintainable automation.
  • Participate in production support and incident response. This includes troubleshooting complex issues across application, cloud, Kubernetes, networking, storage, and infrastructure layers.
  • Contribute to infrastructure and platform design discussions, identify implementation and operational tradeoffs, and seek guidance when decisions have broader architectural, security, or product impact.
  • Apply security and reliability practices throughout infrastructure and software delivery, including access controls, secrets management, change validation, testing, rollback, and deployment safeguards.
  • Participate in the full engineering lifecycle: requirements refinement, design, development, code review, testing, deployment, monitoring, production support, and operational improvement.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly to accelerate automation and engineering work, improve code and configuration quality, assist troubleshooting and testing, and increase team effectiveness. Apply appropriate security and quality controls.
  • Collaborate effectively with software engineers, infrastructure teams, security teams, and other cross-functional partners. Communicate technical and operational decisions clearly, and contribute to engineering documentation and runbooks.



You're Our Person If...

  • 6+ years of experience in a senior or lead role in Cloud DevOps engineering.
  • Experience in performance engineering and benchmarking.
  • Experience designing, deploying, or operating production workloads on public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • Experience developing production software in Core Java, Python, or another object-oriented programming language.
  • Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure concepts, including compute, storage, networking, load balancing, identity and access management, security, high availability, and disaster recovery.
  • Experience with containerization and cloud-native technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, or comparable container orchestration platforms.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code and configuration automation using tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, Helm, or comparable tooling.
  • Experience building, maintaining, or improving CI/CD pipelines and automated build, test, deployment, and release workflows.
  • Development or automation experience using Python, Go, Java, or another programming language. You can build maintainable, production-quality automation, tools, services, or APIs.
  • Familiarity with databases (Postgres, HBase, Oracle, or similar) and database cluster technologies such as Oracle RAC (Real Application Clusters).
  • Experience with Linux systems and working knowledge of operating systems, networking, process, memory, storage, and performance fundamentals.
  • Experience with production observability using logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alerting platforms.
  • Understanding of distributed-system and reliability concepts, including scalability, fault tolerance, resiliency, service dependencies, capacity, availability, and performance.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex production issues across application, infrastructure, networking, and cloud layers.
  • Experience working across the software and infrastructure delivery lifecycle: design, implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools or techniques for automation, software development, troubleshooting, testing, debugging, or documentation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to diagnose complex infrastructure and production problems systematically.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate across engineering and operational teams.



Even Better If...

  • Experience operating large-scale distributed systems or high-availability production platforms.
  • Experience with Kubernetes ecosystem technologies, service discovery, ingress, service mesh, autoscaling, or container platform engineering.
  • Experience building internal developer platforms, self-service infrastructure, deployment frameworks, or operational automation.
  • Experience developing backend services, APIs, command-line tools, controllers, operators, or automation frameworks.
  • Experience with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices, including service level objectives (SLOs), service level indicators (SLIs), error budgets, capacity management, and incident management.
  • Experience with cloud security, IAM, secrets management, vulnerability management, policy enforcement, and infrastructure security controls.
  • Experience with observability technologies such as Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Splunk, or comparable platforms.
  • Experience with databases, caching systems, messaging platforms, or distributed data infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with multi-region, multi-cloud, disaster recovery, or large-scale cloud migration architectures.
  • Familiarity with Agile development practices and iterative release cycles.

The Experience


Slack is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join the Data Infrastructure team within the broader Data Engineering organization. The mission of our team is to build secure, reliable, performant, scalable, and cost-efficient infrastructure with an AI-forward approach that powers Slack’s data ecosystem. We design and operate the core data platforms that enable data engineers, analysts, and machine learning practitioners to deliver trusted insights and data products across Slack.


Our systems power critical workflows — from batch and streaming ingestion to real-time analytics and orchestration. We’re looking for strong technical leaders who can combine hands-on expertise with strategic impact and mentorship-driven leadership to scale, and evolve the backbone of Slack’s data infrastructure.


What You’ll Actually Be Doing:

You’ll play a key role in the design, development, and operation of services that underpin data ingestion, transformation, storage, compute and orchestration at a massive scale. As a Staff Engineer, you’ll be a Directly Responsible Individual (DRI) for multiple core data services, accountable for uptime, reliability, and performance, and a subject matter expert (SME) across multiple systems. Here are a few examples of what we work on:


  • Scaling our compute and orchestration layer with an AI-forward and data driven approach.
  • Enabling more realtime OLAP capabilities for internal and external customers
  • Creating and scaling agents, AI skills, and automation to enable engineers and users on their workflow and data needs
  • What you will be doing
  • Design, build, and operate reliable and scalable data infrastructure powering Slack’s analytics, ML, and data-driven decision-making.
  • Serve as DRI for multiple core data services specifically on our analytics infrastructure (e.g. Pinot, and Trino), ensuring uptime, reliability, and our compute and orchestration services (e.g., Airflow, Spark on Kubernetes, EMR, Hive Metastore).
  • Drive improvements in security, cost efficiency, and developer experience across our data infrastructure.
  • Build automation and self-service tools that empower our team and other data teams to easily adopt and manage data workflows.
  • Collaborate closely with data engineering, platform, and security teams to design scalable, well-governed solutions.
  • Build and enhance our observability, monitoring, and alerting on our services via Grafana and related tooling.
  • Partner with other staff and senior engineers to define best practices, technical standards, and support models for Slack’s data ecosystem.
  • Mentor and coach other engineers, modeling ownership, collaboration, and operational excellence.

You’re Our Person If...:

  • 10+ years of software, platform, or infrastructure engineering experience, including time spent supporting data-intensive systems or data platforms.
  • First-class communication skills and the ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams.
  • Proven experience in building, deploying, and operating distributed infrastructure at scale.
  • Strong technical background with big data and infrastructure technologies — such as EMR, Airflow, Pinot, Trino, Hive Metastore, Kubernetes, or equivalent systems.
  • Proficiency in Python, Golang, Bash, and SQL.
  • Proficiency with CI/CD (GitHub Actions), Vault, Terraform, Chef, and Grafana.
  • Deep understanding of infrastructure reliability, observability, and cost efficiency principles.
  • Hands-on experience supporting data pipelines or data engineering workflows is a strong plus.
  • A strong sense of ownership and a drive to deliver high-impact, autonomous results.

Even Better If...:

  • Hands-on experience building, managing, and integrating agentic workflows, custom AI skills, automated software factory pipelines, MCP
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

What we value

Slack has a positive, diverse, and supportive culture—we look for people who are curious, inventive, and collaborative. We seek engineers who care deeply about craftsmanship, reliability, and empowering others. In our work together, we strive to be smart, humble, hardworking, and—above all—collaborative.

Your Impact

  • Lead deep technical and business discovery sessions with federal stakeholders to uncover mission gaps, pain points, and legacy bottlenecks to scope agentic solution use cases, translate outcomes/ROI into an executable architecture, demonstration/proof-of-concept (POC) and activation plan

  • Drive activation by partnering with customers on agent definition, configuration, and deployment strategy to accelerate production readiness
  • Identify automation and process improvement opportunities by intaking both process and technical requirements to remove friction and accelerate activation
  • Build reusable accelerators (demo environments, components, POC assets, playbooks, best practices) and enable others to scale delivery

  • Leverage modern 3rd-party development tools and AI-assisted coding to rapidly build and iterate on platform configurations, front-end experiences and custom components.

  • Degree in Computer Science required (B.S., Master's, or Ph.D.)
  • Proficiency of Salesforce Core (Public Sector Solutions, Sales, Service, Experience Cloud) and the Data 360/Agentforce stack.

  • The ability to run technical & business discovery to define agentic solution use cases, success metrics, and a feasible execution plan.
  • Executive + technical communication: able to lead whiteboards and communicate with developers and C-suite with equal fluency, and translate architecture to outcomes/ROI.

  • Growth mindset; willingness to continually sharpen technical/advisory skills through required enablement, labs, courses, and certifications.
  • US Citizenship Required

descriptionHtml:

Job Details

About Salesforce

The Experience


The Renewals Team is responsible for managing and forecasting the entire book of renewals business. They forecast and track renewals trends and highlight adoption issues for the company.

The Renewals team partners with sales, customer success manager and support to execute retention strategy. They are responsible for conducting account review, risk assessment and due diligence while developing a renewal strategy. Renewal team members take ownership and maintenance of all renewal opportunities (direct customers and indirect through resellers), forecasting, negotiation, generate upsell/cross sell opportunities, engaging internal resources and closing renewals prior to contract expiration.

As a Scale Renewals Manager you start to handle a large number of renewals. Volume of contracts managed each month tends to be around 50 ~ 100(depends on assigned territory) for Direct and Reseller’s customers in Japan, Korea and Taiwan. You own driving the renewal to completion. You partner with the account team and develop a renewals strategy for every customer. You build quotes, review contract terms, negotiate pricing, look for up-sell opportunities, and handle objections. It is also needed to plan how to improve the current operation process and manage some contractors or outsource partners who are doing renewal management for small size of contracts .

You will be measured on renewal rate, contract term length, and KSO (Key Strategic Objectives) driving specific sales goals of your renewals and ability to negotiate favorable terms.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Drive all managed renewals thoroughly in assigned territory by identify risk as early as possible as well as generating revenue growth opportunity via add-on, upsell, upgrade, price adjustment (working location is Japan Tokyo Office)
  • Achieve or exceed monthly renewal targets and provide senior management with an accurate forecast and risk analysis of all assigned accounts
  • Develop and execute win/win negotiation strategies for contract renewals that maximize contract value while protecting and enhancing the customer relationship
  • Build strong working relationships across Sales and Customer Success Group Leadership
  • Closely monitor at risk accounts. Work with Customer Success, Support, and Services leadership to resolve customer issues and help remove barriers for the team
  • Serve as point of escalation for critical customer issues; provide summary of the overall ‘health’ of the account and use of our services
  • Answer customer questions and successfully negotiate issues related to renewal contracts
  • Attend and lead monthly regional calls to discuss renewal forecast, top renewals, at risk accounts (if required)
  • Managing some contractors or outsource partners to deal with high transaction volume customers.
  • Help develop and educate renewal best practices across the team
  • Maximize account growth opportunities by playing an active role on the account team and helping to identify upsell/cross-sell opportunities upon contract renewal
  • Own, drive and manage the renewals process in collaboration with the account team
  • Work with internal resources (Competitive Intelligence, Pricing, Product Management, Customer Success, Account Executives, etc…) to develop comprehensive ‘win’ strategies for renewals
  • Identify customer requirements, uncover roadblocks, and demonstrate strong account management capabilities to drive renewal to on-time closure
  • Communicate risk clearly and take the lead in developing resolution strategies
  • Accurately maintain a rolling 180 day weekly forecast of renewals of your territory



You're Our Person If...

  • High-level fluency in Japanese language (speaking, reading, writing, listening)
  • High-level fluency in Korean or Chinese language (speaking, reading, writing, listening)
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills (TOEIC 730+ )
  • 3 years or relative experience or sales/account and/or renewal management experience from a software or SI/solution Selling industry are preferable.
  • Vast knowledge or experience of Business Application (CRM/SFA/MA experience as user/sales is preferable)
  • Fundamental understanding of Salesforce product solutions
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Considerable interpersonal skills are mandatory, including the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with others
  • Strong negotiation skills that allow for value-based contract negotiations
  • Knowledge of restructuring contract term and condition relating legal, finance and billing
  • Excellent computer skills (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Google Apps)
  • Degree or Relevant Work Experience Preferred



Leadership Qualities

  • PASSION: Passionate about Customer Success
  • BEGINNERS MIND: Always learning, approaches each interaction with open mind, great listener and hands-on
  • LEADERSHIP: Self-aware and strategic thinker; proficient at building strong relationships
  • TEAM PLAYER: Proficient at collaboration and working with members of a team
  • URGENCY: Ability to move fast and drive business value and results
  • OHANA: Embodies Aloha culture: A team player that everyone enjoys working with and has a generous heart
  • TRUST: Trust the company’s core values
  • ADAPTABLE: Excels in high levels of uncertainty and change

【セールスフォース・ジャパンの働きがいとダイバーシティ】
株式会社セールスフォース・ジャパンは、Great Place To Work® Institute Japan（GPTW）が発表した2026年版「働きがいのある会社」女性ランキングにおいて第2位に初ランクイン、また大規模部門（1,000人以上）においても第3位に選出されました。
弊社では「Equality（平等）」をコアバリューの一つとして掲げ、性別やライフステージに関わらず、すべての社員が能力を最大限に発揮できるインクルーシブな環境づくりを推進しています。社内コミュニティ「Salesforce Women’s Network（SWN）」をはじめとするネットワーキングやキャリア形成支援、メンターシップ制度も活発に稼働しています。

【働き方・ワークライフバランスの推進】
ハイブリッドワーク / リモートワーク制度: 業務内容やチームの取り決めに応じた在宅勤務（リモートワーク）とオフィス勤務の柔軟な組み合わせが可能です。

descriptionHtml:

Job Category

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

As Salesforce adoption grows across regulated industries and the public sector in Australia, customers want more than a description of our security posture. They want a technical Salesforce security counterpart who can design, configure and show the controls that protect their data on the platform. The Manager – Office of the CISO sits within Salesforce's Global Office of the CISO function. It is the hands-on technical voice of Salesforce Security in the region. The role connects our trust posture with how customers actually implement it, turning security, privacy, resilience and compliance commitments into architectures, configurations and evidence that customer CISOs, architects, auditors and regulators can rely on.

This is a customer-facing technical role and an individual contributor position with no direct reports. The successful candidate will spend much of their time with customer security and architecture teams, both whiteboarding and inside the platform. They will design secure Salesforce architectures, configure and demonstrate security controls, and work with the Trust & Security Advisors, Solution Engineers and Technical Architects on strategic deals and implementation

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Lead platform security and security architecture discussions and work with enterprise architects and security engineering teams across enterprise, financial services, critical infrastructure and public-sector accounts.
  • Design and document secure reference architectures for identity, data protection, network connectivity, integration security, logging and monitoring, resilience, and AI/agent security.
  • Map customer security requirements and regulatory obligations, platform controls, configurations and shared-responsibility boundaries.
  • Find gaps between a customer's current security posture on Salesforce, and recommend a practical, prioritised roadmap to close them.
  • Configure, demonstrate and build proofs-of-concept for Salesforce security capabilities, including
  • Identity & Access: SSO (SAML, OpenID Connect), OAuths / External Client Apps, session and login policies, IP restrictions, permission set and profile design, and least-privilege models
  • Data Security: Sharing and visibility architecture, Platform Encryption (including BYOK and cache-only keys), Data Mask, Data Detect and classification.
  • Monitoring & Detection: Event Monitoring, Real-Time Detections, Security Policies, Field Audit Trail, Security Center and Health Check
  • Infrastructure & Connectivity: Hyperforce (including Private Connect, mTLS, and certificate and key management.
  • AI Security: The Einstein / Agentforce Trust Layer, agent permissions and guardrails, prompt and data-grounding controls, and audit AI interactions.
  • Build reusable demo orgs, configuration playbooks, security baselines and hardening guides that the field and partners can use at scalReview customer org configurations against security be expectations, and give clear remediation guidance.
  • Act as the technical security SME on strategic opportunities, discovery sessions and technical validation alongside Solution Engineers and Account teams
  • Serve as the escalation point for complex technical questionnaires, tender/RFP responses and regulated-customer due diligence, especially architecture, encryption, identity, logging and integration security
  • Train Solution Engineers, Technical Architects, Professional Services on secure design patterns and platform security capabilities.
  • Consolidate customer technical requirements and feed them into security product roadmap with Product Management and Engineering.
  • Contribute to technical collateral: reference architectures, whitepapers, best-practice guides, blogs, and conference and customer-summit sessions.
  • Support the Trust & Security Advisors and Government Affairs with technical input on industry and government consultations covering privacy, cyber security, operational resilience and AI



You're Our Person If...

  • Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) and 8–13 years in information, security architecture or security engineering, including significant hands-on design and implementation work in customer-facing or consulting roles
  • Hands-on security architecture. Proven experience in designing enterprise architectures across identity, data protection, network, integration and logging domains, with architecture diagrams and design documents to show for it.
  • Identity & Access Management. Deep practical knowledge of SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect, MFA, federation and privileged access patterns, and how to configure them securely
  • Data protection. Hands-on experience with encryption a management (KMS/HSM, BYOK/HYOK), TLS/mTLS, PKI, data masking and data classification
  • Platform security configuration. Experience configuring SaaS or cloud platforms (Salesforce strongly preferred; ServiceNow, Microsoft 365/Entra, Workday or similar also relevant), including role and permission models, sharing and visibility, and audit logging.
  • Cloud security. Fluency in AWS, GCP and/or Azure security architectures and native controls: IAM, VPC/private connectivity, KMS, CloudTrail and equivalents.
  • Detection & response. Hands-on experience with SIEM tooling (Splunk, Google Chronicle/SecOps, Microsoft Sentinel or similar), log analysis and incident investigation.
  • Application & integration security. Solid understanding of API security, OWASP Top 10, OWASP API Top 10, secure coding practices, and how to interpret penetration test and vulnerability assess
  • Working knowledge of industry security and compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001 family, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, CSA STAR), and the ability to map technical controls to them.
  • Understanding of the Australian regulatory landscape for privacy, cyber security, operational resilience and government security, and how those requirements translate into technical controls.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence. Able to explain complex architecture to a CISO and then go deep on configuration with their engineering team, on live calls and in workshops
  • Strong team player who works well across Product, Engineering, Field, Legal, Privacy and Partners.



Even Better If...

  • Hands-on Salesforce platform experience: Org/Sandbox management, Shield (Platform Encryption, Event Monitoring, Field Audit Trail), Security Center, Hyperforce, Private Connect, and familiarity with Apex, Flows, and integration patterns.
  • Salesforce certifications such as Identity and Access Management Architect, Sharing and Visibility Architect, Security & Privacy, Accredited Professional, Platform Administrator, Application/Systems Architect or a willingness to earn them after joining.
  • Security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CCSK, OSCP, AWS/GCP/Azure Security Specialty, or SANS/GIAC
  • Experience securing AI and LLM workloads: prompt injections, data leakage, agent permissions, and AI governance frameworks.
  • Prior pre-sales, solution engineering or security consulting experience with large enterprise, financial services, critical infrastructure or public-sector customers in Australia.
  • Experience supporting government security assessments or public-sector procurement processes.
  • Practical use of AI tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot, Cursor documentation, configuration review and log analysis.
  • Experience speaking at industry conferences or publishing technical security content.

descriptionHtml:

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

AI agents are changing how enterprise software is built and bought. A new generation of AI-native companies is building the agents, models and tools that businesses will run on, and to scale they need trusted customer data, enterprise distribution and governance. Salesforce is well placed to provide all three.

Our platform holds the customer data and workflows of more than 150,000 companies. With AIforce, our platform for building AI agents, and Headless 360, which gives any AI agent secure access to Salesforce data and actions, that data can power agents whether they run inside Salesforce or on another platform.

We are building the AI partner ecosystem for this next era, and we want an AI ecosystem builder to lead it outside the US.

You will be the first dedicated AI ecosystem partner development manager for our international markets, working alongside a Partner Development Manager who builds the volume side of the partner portfolio. You will find the AI-native companies that matter most to enterprise customers, recruit them as partners, and structure agreements that work for both sides, from fast onboarding to multi-year commercial deals. The partners you sign in your first year will form the foundation of the ecosystem. This is a build role: there is no existing territory, partner book or pipeline to inherit. You will create the target list, pipeline and operating rhythm from scratch, and you will do the work yourself, from cold outreach to closing deals.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Build a portfolio of strategic AI partners outside the US from zero, and run every deal yourself, from cold outreach to signed agreement and live integration.
  • Own your opportunities in Salesforce and run commercial negotiations with high-value partners through to signature.
  • Build joint value propositions with partner product and executive teams, including how their product works alongside Salesforce's own AI products.
  • Assess each partner's strategic position and shape the deal to match.
  • Work with the Partner Solutions team to close them.
  • After signing, run each strategic partnership: joint plans, customer adoption and quarterly business reviews.
  • Prospect yourself every week through cold calls, cold emails and LinkedIn outreach, as well as through venture capital firms, accelerators and founder communities.
  • Recruit partners onto AIforce and AgentExchange (our marketplace for AI agents and agent actions), and onboard them through our partner programme.
  • Find companies already integrating with Salesforce, including through Headless 360 and our Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and convert those relationships into governed commercial partnerships.
  • Help design new commercial models as the platform evolves
  • Build co-sell motions with Salesforce's regional sales teams so partner solutions appear in customer deals, and track partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline.
  • Bring partners to market: joint customer stories, AgentExchange listings and events such as Dreamforce and World Tours.
  • Bring partner and customer feedback to Salesforce product teams to shape the AIforce and Headless 360 roadmap.
  • Work alongside the Partner Development Manager, AI Ecosystem, and help set the recruitment approach and onboarding playbook for the wider partner portfolio.
  • Work with Salesforce account executives, solution engineers, product, legal and alliances teams, and with US business development counterparts.
  • Keep an accurate pipeline in Salesforce and report progress, risks and market signals to leadership.



You're Our Person If...

  • ISV partnership experience: 7+ years (or equivalent experience) in partnerships or business development, recruiting software companies onto a platform or marketplace, negotiating partner agreements, and running integration, listing and co-sell programmes.
  • AI partnership expertise: at least 3 of those years leading partnerships with AI-native companies building agents, models or AI developer tools, at an AI lab, an AI-native ISV or platform, or a hyperscaler's AI partner team. You can name the ISV and AI partnerships you closed.
  • Working knowledge of how AI agents are built and connected: LLMs, agent orchestration, tool calling and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar integration standards. You can hold a credible technical conversation with a startup CTO.
  • Experience structuring partner economics for AI products: consumption or usage-based pricing, marketplace revenue share, or paid access to tools and APIs.
  • Experience building a partner ecosystem or programme from an early stage, not only managing established relationships.
  • An existing network in the AI startup and scale-up community outside the US, including founders, product leaders, venture capital firms and accelerators.
  • Comfortable with data: you build and maintain your own pipeline and partner performance reporting.
  • A hands-on, self-starting approach: you prospect, run and close deals yourself, with little structure around you, across several countries and cultures.
  • Executive presence: you can lead a negotiation with a founder or CEO and present a business case to senior Salesforce leaders.
  • Clear written communication, including deal memos and business cases for senior leaders.



Even Better If...

  • Experience with the Salesforce ecosystem: AppExchange, ISV partner programmes or AIforce.
  • Background at a hyperscaler, AI platform company or AI-native startup.
  • Technical background (engineering, product management or solutions engineering) or hands-on experience building with AI agents, MCP servers or developer tools.
  • Experience co-selling with the field sales teams of a hyperscaler or SaaS platform.
  • Experience in conversational or voice AI, workflow automation, data providers or developer tools.
  • Familiarity with the regulation shaping enterprise AI adoption, such as GDPR and EU data residency, the EU AI Act, and requirements in regulated sectors like financial services.

descriptionHtml:

Our Futureforce University Recruiting program is dedicated to attracting, retaining and cultivating talent. Our interns and new graduates work on real projects that affect how our business runs, giving them the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the future of our company. With offices all over the world, our recruits have the chance to collaborate and connect with fellow employees on a global scale. We offer job shadowing, mentorship programs, talent development courses, and much more.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Help build the next generation of AI-powered engineering. Join our AI-native Academy as an early-career Software Engineer (AMTS) to solve real production challenges, build intelligent automation and strengthen system reliability. With hands-on guidance from a senior mentor, you’ll combine software development with production support experience, building the skills to grow into broader product and platform engineering roles.


You’ll investigate support cases, troubleshoot production issues and participate in support rotations—gaining firsthand insight into how complex systems work and where they can improve. Your mandate goes beyond resolving individual issues: you’ll build software, AI agents and tools that eliminate recurring manual work and prevent problems from returning.


Your projects could include agentic Tier 1/2 case automation, automated access workflows, technical knowledge retrieval, log analysis and system hardening. You’ll write, test, review and deploy code, with opportunities to own improvements from identifying the problem to measuring the result.


As you demonstrate strong engineering skills and measurable impact, you’ll have opportunities to graduate into core product engineering teams, based on your readiness and business needs. It’s a chance to learn through practical ownership, deliver meaningful improvements and build a foundation for your software engineering career.


What you’ll do

  • Investigate and resolve support cases, production defects, access issues and integration failures.
  • Build automation for recurring tasks such as access requests, case responses, log analysis, troubleshooting and maintenance.
  • Develop AI agents and workflows that help classify cases, retrieve relevant knowledge and execute approved actions with appropriate safeguards.
  • Identify root causes and improve code, monitoring, tests and documentation to prevent recurring incidents.
  • Write, test, review and deploy maintainable software using established engineering practices.
  • Participate in incident response and scheduled support or on-call rotations, with training and guidance appropriate to your experience.
  • Work with senior mentors and product teams to understand systems, prioritize improvements and deliver changes safely.
  • Measure the impact of your work through reduced manual effort, fewer repeat issues, faster resolution and improved reliability.

What you’ll bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in computer science, engineering or a related field.
  • Foundational programming skills in at least one language, such as Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript or Go.
  • An understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, APIs, testing, version control and debugging.
  • An ability to investigate problems using logs, error messages and system behavior.
  • Curiosity about automation, AI-assisted development and reliable production systems.
  • Clear communication, a collaborative approach and a willingness to ask questions and learn from feedback.
  • We welcome evidence of your skills from internships, coursework, personal projects, open-source contributions or professional experience. The scope and independence expected will reflect the level of the role.

Helpful experience

  • Building scripts, internal tools or workflow automation.

The Experience

Join the Seller Analytics team in Salesforce's Digital Enterprise Technology organization. We build and run the Sales Data Mesh: our governed, certified data products for Sales, covering our Pipeline Metrics, Annual Order Value, AE and Product Participation, Product Usage, and more. Our consumers are the CRO Analytics team, sales leaders across the globe, and our partner analytics teams in Finance, Revenue, and Marketing.
Our consumers rely on those data products, and this role keeps them trustworthy. You are the first responder; when a consumer reports that a number looks wrong, a dashboard is stale, or a pipeline did not land, you reproduce the problem, find the cause, and resolve-or-route it with a clear writeup. It is an investigate-and-triage role first. Over the first year we will train you to move from operating the mesh to building it, growing into a data engineering role. We are hiring for someone who wants that path.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Triage issues reported by consumers in Slack support channels. Reproduce the problem, establish the grain and definitions involved, and give a clear answer or next step.
  • Investigate data-quality and freshness problems across the bronze to gold layers. Trace a wrong or missing number back to the model, source, or pipeline run that caused it.
  • Run row-level and column-level validation and parity checks when models change or legacy logic is migrated, and confirm the results match.
  • Watch monitoring and alerting (Monte Carlo, dbt tests, source freshness) and act on failures. Open and track the work in Linear.
  • Support hypercare and UAT for launches and migrations. Verify fixes in Snowflake and keep stakeholders updated on status.
  • Keep definitions, grain, and known issues documented so the next question is faster to answer.

Where This Role Grows

  • This is an operate-and-support role today, with a deliberate path into data engineering. As you build SQL and dbt depth, you will take on model changes and tests, and in time build and own mesh data products. If you want to become a data engineer, this role is built for that.

You're Our Person If…

  • You are proficient in Tableau Desktop and/or SQL and can read, debug, and validate queries against real data.
  • You have an investigate-and-triage instinct. You are comfortable not knowing the answer yet and work a problem methodically until you find the cause.
  • You are comfortable in Snowflake or a similar cloud data warehouse.
  • You communicate clearly in writing and can explain a data issue, its cause, and its fix to a non-engineer.
  • You want to grow into data engineering and are ready to be trained on the rest.

Even Better If…

  • You have used dbt or a similar transformation framework.
  • You have worked with data observability or monitoring tools (e.g. Monte Carlo).
  • You understand dimensional modeling, grain, and surrogate keys.
  • You have done migration or parity work: replacing legacy logic and proving the new results match.
  • You have used Airflow, Tableau, or Snowflake semantic views and Cortex.
  • You have used AI-assisted engineering tools such as Claude Code.

The Experience

We're looking for a Distinguished Solution Engineer to join Salesforce's UK Public Sector, leading on our most strategic accounts. This is a senior individual contributor role at the intersection of business consulting, technical credibility, and customer strategy - working with the UK's most significant Government organisations. The Public Sector differs from other industries, yet can benefit as much or even more from Salesforce technology and expertise - transforming the citizen experience and improving society.

You'll partner closely with the Account Team, Government CTO function, FDE organisation, product teams, and customers to shape how Salesforce's platform and AI capabilities can transform how the Public Sector engages with their citizens, businesses and drive operational change. You'll be a trusted advisor, a hands-on builder, and a commercial thinker - often in the same conversation.

This isn't a role for someone who presents slides and moves on. It's for someone who digs into the customer's world, earns the right to be in the room at senior levels, and turns complex problems into compelling, credible solutions. Modern citizen experiences rely on connected data, AI, automation, and digital engagement. These experiences require integrated architectures that leverage the breadth of the Salesforce Platform alongside enterprise applications, data platforms, integration technologies, and partner ecosystems - with your knowledge, experience and skill used to bring it to life.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Lead technical and business discovery across our largest and most important public sector accounts - running workshops, stakeholder sessions, and structured problem-solving to uncover the real challenge behind the stated one.
  • Build trusted partnerships with Sales - acting as a genuine co-pilot to the Account Team, contributing commercial instinct alongside technical expertise, and showing up as a proactive, high-performing teammate in the deals that matter most.
  • Shape and deliver solution strategies that connect Salesforce's multi-product platform to the specific priorities of the UK Government's largest organisations, supporting millions of citizens and tens of thousands of employees.
  • Build and demonstrate - whether that's a polished executive demo, a rapid prototype, or a hands-on proof of concept. You use working examples to make the story real.
  • Develop AI and data points of view relevant to the Public Sector context: agentic workflows, grounding and RAG architecture, Agentforce use cases, and how organisations can govern and scale AI responsibly within policy, guidance and regulatory constraints.
  • Demonstrate value throughout the Government procurement process - working with senior technical stakeholders including C-suite, board-level sponsors and beyond to prove the value of the Salesforce platform across multiple lines of business
  • Orchestrate internal resources - coordinating and leading specialists, product SMEs, the builder organisation and delivery expertise at the right moments, and leaving teams better informed through what you share.
  • Contribute to the SE community — sharing knowledge, raising the bar on what good looks like, and helping develop the broader Global Public Sector SE capability.



You're Our Person If...

  • Degree or equivalent relevant experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the core proficiencies of the role (e.g. extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience, etc.)
  • Relevant 10+ years of experience in the IT Industry, either pre-sales or implementation of customer engagement solutions, supporting the sales cycle in selling CRM or high value business solutions.
  • Strong grasp of enterprise technology architecture: cloud platforms, APIs, integration patterns, data infrastructure, and identity/security considerations., with extensive experience designing solutions for complex business and technology environments.
  • Proven ability to engage at C-level with both business and technology audiences — adapting fluently between commercial framing and technical depth.
  • Excellent communication skills: structured, clear, and audience-aware. You write well, you present with conviction, and you know when to listen.
  • A working understanding of AI and its application in enterprise organizations - including how large language models, agentic workflows, and AI-driven automation are reshaping customer engagement, operations, and compliance. You don't need to be a data scientist, but you should be able to hold a credible conversation about what's possible and what's practical.

    Even Better If...
  • Hands-on experience with agentic AI tools and practices — Claude Code, Cursor, Agentforce, or equivalent — and the ability to build as well as advise.
  • Experience with Salesforce Industry Clouds, preferably Public Sector Solutions, Data Cloud, Salesforce Platform and the Agentforce AI platform.
  • Experience with design thinking, value-based selling, executive consulting, and enterprise transformation initiatives.
  • Salesforce certifications (Administrator, Platform Developer, AI Specialist or similar).
  • A track record of building or contributing to reusable assets — demo environments, competitive frameworks, industry-specific POVs — that elevate the team beyond a single deal.



What We're Really Looking For

You'll bring enough industry knowledge to be taken seriously in senior conversations, enough curiosity to keep learning as the landscape shifts, a proactive mindset and hands on attitude, delivering demos, prototypes as well as you would executive presentations, and enough clarity in how you communicate to make complex ideas land with any audience.

You'll do well here if you:

  • Prepare thoroughly - you think through the customer's world before you walk into it, and that preparation shows.
  • Build when it helps - you reach for a working example when words alone won't make the story real.

descriptionHtml:

Position Overview

As a Cloud Success Training Strategist for Commerce with cross-cloud coverage, you set the training strategy for the Commerce customer training ecosystem and for the additional product areas you are asked to support. You connect product direction, customer needs, business priorities, and training evidence to decide where and how Salesforce Training & Certification should invest, and you act as a business advisor who translates business goals into a training strategy with a defensible rationale.


You are a strategic partner to Cloud Success leadership, using data to recommend the most effective training interventions. Your mission is to bridge product innovation and customer value realization, with an emphasis on supporting product adoption and customer retention. You do this in partnership with your functional partners in Curriculum Development, Delivery, and Operations, who own the staffing and execution of the work.


Role scope: Commerce remains the primary area of ownership. Additional cross-cloud coverage is assigned based on business priorities and available capacity, with scope and commitments reviewed regularly. When new areas are introduced, existing priorities and responsibilities are reassessed to ensure a manageable portfolio. This is a defining feature of the role, not a temporary arrangement. The expectations of the role do not change with the areas you cover: the core responsibilities and the definition of success are the same for every area, and you apply them to whichever areas you are asked to support. We are looking for a senior-level strategist who is adaptable across a changing product portfolio and clear about what excellence looks like.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership & Business Alignment


  • Training Strategy & Annual Plan: Draft and own the training strategy and annual plan (our V2MOM goal-setting framework) for each area you cover, aligned to Cloud Success leaders' priorities, with shared measures co-owned with those leaders.
  • Executive Advisory: Act as a specialist partner to Cloud Success leadership, giving data-backed recommendations on training investment, modality, and timing. When a request would be better served another way, make the case with evidence. Where disagreement remains, document the evidence and trade-offs and escalate through established leadership channels.
  • Business Reviews: Act as the primary training representative in Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews, presenting training impact data, feature adoption trends, and roadmap alignment.
  • Shared Commitments: Establish mutual commitments with Cloud Success leaders and escalate unmet dependencies.
  • Product & Success Integration: Partner with Product, Success, and customer-facing teams to translate product direction, customer feedback, and learning barriers into training strategies that support adoption and customer success. For Commerce, this includes the B2C and B2B Commerce product lines and Agentforce-enabled Commerce capabilities.

Emerging Product Coverage

  • Emerging Product Areas: Set training strategy for emerging or fast-moving product areas beyond Commerce, as assigned by leadership based on current business priorities, using the same standards you apply to your primary domain. Ramp quickly as coverage areas change.
  • Cross-Cloud Themes: Partner with other strategists on themes that span clouds (for example Agentforce and shared platform capabilities) so customers see a coherent training path.
  • Adaptive Prioritization: Work with leadership to revisit what you cover periodically, making the trade-offs between Commerce commitments and emerging needs visible.

Portfolio Strategy & Planning

  • Demand & Capacity Signal: Forecast demand, recommend portfolio priorities and trade-offs, and communicate capacity needs to functional partners. Raise gaps and risks early so leadership can make an informed decision.
  • Cadence & Modality: Recommend frequency, cadence, time-zone coverage, and modality mix, from high-touch instructor-led sessions to scalable digital formats, to get the highest return on training resources.
  • Awareness & Reach: Proactively partner with Cloud Success and Marketing to drive training awareness and reach.
  • Performance Diagnosis: When audience reach, engagement, or class fill rates (seats filled versus capacity) fall short, lead the cross-functional synthesis of evidence (relevance of the training, delivery timing, awareness) and recommend a strategic response with the functional partners that own execution.
  • Risk Visibility: Make dependencies, risks, and unmet commitments visible, and escalate unresolved decisions on time.

Training Lifecycle & Data-Driven Decisioning

  • Strategic Blueprint: Define the strategic need and direction for training initiatives in a Strategic Blueprint: the business justification, target audience, desired outcomes, and strategic acceptance criteria. Curriculum Development owns instructional design, outlines, and production, while the strategist stays engaged as priorities and customer needs evolve, consulting at defined gates.
  • Portfolio Evaluation: Lead recurring evaluation of the training catalog using a structured framework that weighs business impact, audience reach, and operational efficiency. Recommend whether to maintain, transform, retire, or invest in assets, using evidence from functional partners. Leadership approves major strategic or capacity implications.
  • Continuous Innovation: Design experiments to test new formats, durations, and engagement tactics, using data to establish what works before it scales.

How Success Is Defined

Success is measured by the quality and impact of the training strategy, with accountability focused on outcomes the strategist can control or influence. The expectations are the same for every area covered.


  • Strategic Alignment: Develop clear, defensible training strategies aligned with business priorities and customer needs, translated into strategic blueprints that Curriculum Development can execute against.
  • Business Partnership: Provide data-driven recommendations that influence training investments and priorities, with trade-offs documented when recommendations are not adopted.
  • Risk Visibility: Surface dependencies, capacity gaps, and unmet commitments early, and escalate them on time.
  • Portfolio Performance: Use performance insights to guide improvements in audience reach, engagement, and effectiveness, in partnership with the teams that own delivery and data.
  • Business Impact: Demonstrate training's contribution to product adoption and customer success through shared measures.

Qualifications

  • Strategic Leadership: 10+ years in Customer Education, Strategic Consulting, or Program Management, with experience architecting large-scale learning programs for complex technical products. Experience with commerce, e-commerce, or retail technology (B2C and/or B2B) highly preferred. 
  • Business Acumen: Proven ability to align departmental strategies with executive-level goals and broad business objectives.
  • Influential Advisory: Ability to build trusted relationships, influence senior stakeholders, and drive cross-functional alignment.
  • Data Literacy: Proficiency in using product usage data and engagement data to drive a roadmap, identify business risks, and demonstrate impact.
  • Operational Planning: Experience forecasting demand and communicating capacity needs across multi-modal delivery strategies in global markets.
  • Cross-Domain Breadth: Ability to ramp quickly on, and balance priorities across, more than one product domain.

Principal, AI & Integrated Solutions Architect — Financial Services

Regulated Industries Architecture · Salesforce · Grade 8

About the role

Our Financial Services Industry Architecture team works on Salesforce’s largest and most complex banking, insurance, and wealth management customers. We don’t stop at showing customers what’s possible; we prove it by building it with them. Success here is a working prototype or a deployed asset, not a great deck.

As a Principal AI & Integrated Solutions Architect, you will be the trusted technical lead for a set of strategic FS accounts. You’ll help design agentic AI architectures that hold up under real scrutiny: governed multi-agent systems, headless and API-first experiences, and unified data and integration patterns that span Agentforce, Data 360, MuleSoft, and the customer’s existing systems. You’ll work across the full engagement. That means framing the problem with C-level and Chief Architect stakeholders, building the prototype that proves the value, and handing it off cleanly to partners and delivery teams so it scales into production and becomes a reusable play for the whole organization.

You’ll sit within an FS segment team and belong to the broader Regulated Industries architecture community. That gives you exposure to patterns and peers across financial services, healthcare, life sciences, and the public sector.

What you’ll do

Lead agentic AI architecture on strategic accounts (≈30%). Serve as the aligned architect for your accounts. Run discovery and org assessments, set the current- and future-state architecture, and own architectural direction from first conversation through production handoff. Shape decisions on agent orchestration, MCP and agent-to-agent interoperability, headless and composable design, data foundations, and the trust and governance layer.

Build to prove value (≈25%). Co-build working prototypes and proof-of-value assets on customers’ own data and objects, using modern AI-assisted development tools. Turn a hypothesis into something a business sponsor can see and use within weeks, not quarters.

Run and extend our engagement plays (≈15%). Deliver our defined engagement models. These cover the economics of an agentic operating model, headless experiences that keep governance intact, governed multi-agent systems at enterprise scale, and executive North Star architecture. Add new content and reusable components back to the shared library, so each engagement leaves the next one further ahead.

Own the handoff and the path to scale (≈10%). Package architecture, data dictionaries, process maps, and agent metadata so that partners, SIs, and delivery teams can take the work to production without losing the design intent. Hold clear entry and exit gates so delivery stays planned and predictable.

Advise executives on FS outcomes (≈10%). Translate architecture into business value for CIOs, CTOs, Chief Architects, and line-of-business leaders. Fit designs to FS regulatory, data residency, model risk, and operating-model constraints. Represent Salesforce at executive briefings, architecture review boards, and industry events.

Elevate the team and the field (≈10%). Mentor architects and account teams. Contribute points of view, reference architectures, and reusable assets. Work closely with AEs, SEs, Professional Services, forward-deployed engineers, partners, and product teams, with each role doing its own job well.

What success looks like
  • Architecture-sourced pipeline and measurable progression on priority opportunities in your accounts.
  • Agentforce and Data 360 consumption milestones reached and tied to customer outcomes.
  • Prototypes that convert into production commitments and reusable plays adopted by other architects.
  • Customers who treat you as their go-to architecture advisor, shown by repeat engagement and sponsorship from executive and Chief Architect stakeholders.
  • Disciplined engagement records, so your impact is visible and credited.
What you’ll bring
  • 10+ years in enterprise or solution architecture, including significant customer-facing work in financial services: banking, insurance, wealth/asset management, or payments.
  • Deep hands-on experience with the Salesforce platform (Financial Services Cloud, Service/Sales Cloud, Data 360) and enterprise integration, ideally MuleSoft and API-led design.
  • Practical, current experience designing and building AI solutions. This includes LLM-based agents, retrieval and grounding, agent orchestration, and emerging interoperability standards such as MCP and A2A.
  • Builder credibility. You personally prototype using code (Apex, JavaScript/Node, Python, or similar) and AI-assisted development tools, and you’re comfortable working in Git-based workflows.
  • Working knowledge of FS regulatory and risk requirements: privacy, data residency, model risk management, auditability, and AI governance. You also know how these requirements shape architecture decisions.
  • Executive presence. You can hold a contested architecture debate with a Chief Architect and move it to a decision.
  • A team-first operating style. You’re comfortable working within aligned coverage, sharing assets, and making others better.
Nice to have
  • Salesforce certifications such as Agentforce Specialist, Data Cloud Consultant, Application/System Architect, or progress toward CTA.
  • Experience on the customer or SI side of large FS transformations.
  • Exposure to process intelligence or agentic operations tooling.
  • Published points of view, conference talks, or open reusable assets.

  • Knowledge of related applications, relational databases, and ERP technologies

descriptionHtml:

About Salesforce

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Role Overview

We are looking for a technically strong Security Governance professional who can bridge the gap between Security & Compliance requirements and Engineering implementation.


This role will serve as the technical voice and face of Assurance. You will partner closely with Engineering organizations, PCLs, Product Security, Legal, and other stakeholders to understand how security and compliance requirements are implemented in real systems. You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.


The successful candidate will understand systems and architectures deeply enough to move beyond validating whether a control exists. They will evaluate how the control is designed, implemented, operated, and scaled across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Bridge Assurance and Engineering - Serve as a technical liaison between Assurance, Engineering, Product Security, PCLs, Legal, and other stakeholders, ensuring governance requirements are technically feasible, understandable, and implementable.
  • Evaluate Control Implementation - Work directly with Engineering teams to understand how security and compliance controls are implemented within applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud environments, and engineering workflows.
  • Create the Engineering Feedback Loop - Assess what is working, what is creating unnecessary friction, and where controls or requirements are unclear or difficult to operationalize. Feed those insights back into control design, standards, and governance processes.
  • Make Requirements Engineer-Usable - Translate regulatory, compliance, and security expectations into clear, actionable technical requirements that Engineering teams can consistently implement and validate.
  • Develop Second-Line Oversight - Develop second-line oversight protocols that independently monitor, audit, and validate that all security controls are operational across engineering teams in Salesforce (e.g., attestations, CRE checks).
  • Understand Systems End-to-End - Develop a deep understanding of key platforms, architectures, engineering processes, security capabilities, and control implementations to help Assurance make better risk and compliance decisions.
  • Assess Risk in M&A - Assess control and risk exposure during M&As. Design the assessment to price risk, evaluate compatibility, and deliver an executable activation plan tied back to the risk model.
  • Partner on Emerging Security Requirements - Collaborate with Product Security, Legal, PCEs, Market Enablement, and other teams to understand emerging requirements and determine how they should translate into future security controls and engineering expectations.
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.
  • Drive Change Management and Enablement - Build the change management, training, and communication needed to shift teams from "go find and interpret a policy" to "know precisely what applies and how to comply."
  • Run Control Incident Management - Stand up a formal incident management practice for control failures. Include postmortems, root-cause analysis, and error budgets for controls, modeled on availability incident response.
  • Influence Future Control Design - Partner with control owners and technical teams to evolve controls based on new technologies, regulatory expectations, architecture changes, and lessons learned from implementation.
  • Drive Security Champion Engagement - Build strong relationships with technical stakeholders across Engineering. Establish a network of security/control champions who can provide implementation feedback, promote requirements, and help scale governance across teams.
  • Report to Executive Leadership - Report on control reliability, coverage, pressure, and systemic risk trends to executive leadership. Feed findings back to the control framework for continuous improvement.
  • Represent Assurance Across Technical Organizations - Act as a trusted technical representative for Assurance in architecture, engineering, security, and governance discussions. Help ensure Assurance is involved early rather than only during audit or compliance validation.

What we're looking for:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required. We're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 5-6 years of relevant experience or technical background in security engineering, cloud security, product security, IAM, platform engineering, or IT governance.
  • Ability to understand complex systems, architectures, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, and software development processes.
  • Experience translating security, risk, regulatory, or compliance requirements into technical implementation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of security controls and frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC, SOX, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with emerging technology and regulatory areas such as AI security, AI governance, privacy, and evolving global technology regulations.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering while also partnering with Legal, Compliance, Security, Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical implementation details to governance teams and translate governance expectations into language Engineering teams can act on.
  • Ability to challenge existing requirements constructively and recommend improvements based on technical realities and risk.
  • Experience with independent control testing, assurance or audit practices, incident or root-cause analysis, or M&A due diligence is a plus.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means creating a strong connection between what Assurance requires and what Engineering can effectively implement. Controls become more technically relevant, and requirements become easier for Engineering teams to consume. Implementation challenges are identified earlier, and emerging security and regulatory expectations are incorporated into the control environment before they become compliance gaps. Control failures are handled with the same rigor as availability incidents, and leadership has clear visibility into control reliability and systemic risk.


Ultimately, this role will help move Assurance from primarily validating compliance to becoming a technical governance partner that actively shapes secure and compliant engineering practices by design.

We empower you to be a Trailblazer, too — driving your performance and career growth, charting new paths, and improving the state of the world. We are looking for exceptional candidates to join the Public Sector ECS Solution Engineering team. The ECS business is the highest performing, highest growth team in Public Sector. As part of the Salesforce Public Sector business unit, we provide PaaS and SaaS cloud solutions to Canadian and US State and Local customers. The Solution Engineer is responsible for presenting our solutions based on the customer’s business and value drivers, seamlessly weaving technology, capabilities and business requirements into every customer presentation. The Solution Engineer is responsible for securing the technical and functional win in every opportunity by addressing the customer’s business requirements and removing all technical objections throughout the sales cycle. To accomplish this, the Solution Engineer must partner closely with Sales and have technology and sales acumen to drive meaningful discovery to undercover current and future state business requirements, develop a technical sales strategy, configure and demonstrate the solutions that address these requirements while focusing on business value.
Prior experience with Customer Relationship Management technology and enterprise selling in a customer-facing role is highly desirable. But equally important is self-drive and motivation to learn new technologies and industries. Solution Engineers are master storytellers; they take complex pieces of technology and explain them in an intuitive and compelling way.

Responsibilities:

  • Understand customer goals and challenges and map those back to the Salesforce product portfolio
  • Design, build, and demonstrate innovative solutions to address these challenges
  • Present Salesforce technology infrastructure, including demonstrating deep familiarity with hardware, software, networking and security stack
  • Participate in all appropriate product, sales, technical training and certifications to acquire and maintain the knowledge necessary to be effective in the position
  • Attain quarterly and annual objectives defined collaboratively with management
  • Respond effectively to RFIs/RFPs
  • Active participation in a fast-paced high-energy market segment and balance multiple projects in a team-selling environment


Minimum Qualifications:

  • 5 years experience as a solution/sales engineer for a CRM company or similar technology
  • Knowledge of AI tools, related applications, relational database, web technology and cyber-security
  • Solid oral, written, presentation and interpersonal communication skills
  • Ability to work as part of a cross-functional team to solve technical problems

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Canadian and/or US Public Sector industry experience
  • Familiarity with Salesforce technology
  • Familiarity with Government Cloud Compliance standards and certifications
  • Work Location: Toronto

title: Backbone Network Engineering Principal
descriptionHtml:

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

  • Infrastructure Architecture (IA) owns the design, security, and evolution of Salesforce's first-party data center network. We architect the routing, switching, firewall, and load-balancing infrastructure behind large-scale sites that span several Salesforce business units. We also own the backbone connectivity to the internet and to our public cloud environments (AWS and GCP). As a Principal Network Engineer, you will set technical direction for this network and lead the security posture of our edge. You will also manage the lifecycle of the hardware and designs behind it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Define and evolve reference architectures for first-party data center networks. These span routers, switches, firewalls, and load balancers, with lighter touchpoints into compute.
  • Design network and application delivery architectures for large-scale sites that serve multiple business units across Salesforce.
  • Own backbone and internet connectivity, plus interconnect between our data centers and public cloud environments (AWS and GCP).
  • Own infrastructure lifecycle for hardware and designs. For example, you might lead a refresh of an aging top-of-rack switch by evaluating and selecting a suitable newer model, then defining the validated design and transition approach.
  • Build and maintain network automation and tooling in Ansible and Python, managed in Git repositories. Use AI models in day-to-day design, development, analysis, and documentation work.
  • Act as a technical authority and escalation point for complex design, capacity, and incident-driven architecture questions.
  • Lead network security architecture, including security feature design and edge hardening. Partner with Network Operations, Security, Supply Chain/Capacity Planning, and cloud teams to deliver at scale. Mentor engineers and influence cross-org technical strategy through design reviews and architectural documentation.
  • Drive deployment and tuning of edge protocols and policy, such as mTLS, HTTP/2, and cipher suite changes.
  • Run software certification and vulnerability and bug management for network platforms, coordinating remediation with vendors and operations teams.

You're Our Person If You Have:


  • 10+ years of experience in network engineering or architecture, with a track record at data center or service-provider scale. Software-driven engineering skills: Ansible, Python, and Git-based development workflows. Vendor familiarity with Cisco, F5, Juniper, and Ciena.
  • Familiarity with liquid cooling and high-density facility considerations (such as direct-to-chip cooling, power and thermal constraints, and rack density) and how they influence network hardware selection, rack layout, and design.
  • AI fluency: hands-on experience and familiarity with AI models, and the ability to apply them effectively in engineering workflows.
  • Proven record of leading multi-team, multi-year architecture efforts.
  • Deep expertise in large-scale data center and WAN/backbone design (BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, L2/L3 fabrics, routing policy). Load balancing and application delivery design experience, particularly with F5 (BIG-IP). This includes certificate management and lifecycle, and how certificates and keys are assigned to virtual servers; SSL/TLS termination and re-encryption design, including client-SSL and server-SSL profiles; SSL and HTTP header handling, such as forwarded client IP and protocol headers; and traffic policy and customization through iRules and related profiles (HTTP, persistence, and others).
  • Hands-on experience with firewalls and TLS termination at the edge.
    Strong security background: vulnerability management, software qualification, and secure protocol configuration. Experience with hardware lifecycle planning, including platform evaluation, refresh, and migration.
  • Experience with new GPU cluster builds, including topology planning, capacity and scale modeling, and coordination with compute, storage, and facilities teams from design through deployment.
  • Clear communication with executives and engineers.

Even Better If you have:

  • Vendor familiarity with Cisco, F5, Juniper, and Ciena.
  • Familiarity with public cloud connectivity (AWS Direct Connect, GCP Interconnect) and hybrid architectures. Knowledge of AI data center network design, including high-bandwidth, low-latency fabrics for GPU clusters (for example InfiniBand or RoCE/Ethernet-based back-end networks) and the front-end/back-end network separation typical of AI workloads.
  • Familiarity with liquid cooling and high-density facility considerations (such as direct-to-chip cooling, power and thermal constraints, and rack density) and how they influence network hardware selection, rack layout, and design.

descriptionHtml:
