The Experience

The REWS Workplace Innovation team is seeking a Workplace Research Manager to serve as the primary owner, operational driver, and analytical engine of our global Site Experience Survey Program. In this individual contributor role, you will bring analytical curiosity, proactive problem-solving, and quantitative rigor to our research, translating employee sentiment datasets into actionable findings that uncover the underlying drivers of workplace experience.

  • Reporting to the Senior Manager, Workplace Research, you will serve as a dedicated survey research partner and subject matter expert across Workplace Innovation teams (Pilots, Space Insights) and other REWS stakeholders.
  • In this role, you will own the global Site Experience Survey Program end-to-end, partnering closely with the Site Study Program Lead and Space Insights team to connect employee sentiment with spatial telemetry and observational data.
  • You will combine an investigative, data-driven mindset with sound survey measurement practices, while adopting AI tools and automated workflows to accelerate synthesis and deliver timely, high-impact insights.
  • This role is based in San Francisco, CA, Chicago, IL, or Atlanta, GA, and is eligible for an Office Flexible (3 days/week) work arrangement, with potential for occasional domestic or international travel for site studies.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

  • Own and execute the global Site Experience Survey Program end-to-end, developing longitudinal benchmarking and driving continuous refinement of survey instruments. Bring proactive analytical curiosity to explore datasets—applying statistical techniques like correlation, regression, key driver analysis, and segmentation—to move beyond descriptive reporting, uncover non-obvious trends across multi-office datasets, and develop data-driven workplace personas.
  • Partner closely with the Site Study Program Lead and Space Insights team to bridge and integrate disparate data streams into strategic site study reports. Connect employee survey sentiment with objective spatial telemetry (such as occupancy patterns and room utilization metrics) to co-develop executive-ready recommendations that guide long-term workplace design, space allocations, and capital investment decisions.
  • Serve as a survey research and questionnaire design subject matter expert across REWS, advising internal teams and project leads on question design, rating scales, and practical sampling strategies across a diverse range of measurement scenarios (e.g., workplace pilot evaluations, guest experience, meeting and event feedback, and pre-design needs assessments).
  • Take hands-on ownership of day-to-day survey operations and data hygiene, configuring, maintaining, and refining templated survey instruments, coordinating with internal communications to manage distribution, and preparing clean datasets for analysis. Partner with the REWS Technology and Data Engineering (TEDI) team to evolve self-serve dashboards, while integrating AI tools to streamline qualitative text analytics.

You’re Our Person If…

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience designing, fielding, and analyzing quantitative surveys within corporate real estate, workplace strategy, environmental psychology, people analytics, or an applied organizational research setting.
  • Demonstrated analytical curiosity and practical quantitative skills (including significance testing, correlation, regression modeling, and key driver analysis) paired with solid survey design fundamentals (scale reliability, questionnaire design) to independently uncover actionable drivers from large, multi-office datasets.
  • Demonstrated experience configuring, updating, and managing survey instruments within enterprise platforms (such as SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, or similar), alongside practical experience cleaning, transforming, and joining datasets (using SQL, Python/pandas, R/tidyverse, Tableau Prep, or similar data workflows) and hands-on proficiency with open-source statistical tools (specifically R or Python) to independently conduct exploratory and inferential analysis.

As a key contributor within the Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) Finance team, you will play a pivotal role in the integration of newly acquired companies into Salesforce. You will be a partner in guiding our acquired businesses through the operational integration journey, ensuring the alignment of financial management and processes, and maximizing value to accelerate growth. By representing the finance team throughout the M&A integration life cycle, you will act as a trusted advisor, advocating for the interests of both Salesforce and the acquired companies.  If you are driven, have a passion for finance and M&A and thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, we encourage you to apply and join our team in shaping the future of Salesforce’s M&A integration efforts.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Serve as a finance point of contact between Salesforce’s matrixed M&A organization and the acquired businesses, building trust with internal partners (e.g., the Salesforce Corporate Development Integration team) and external partners (e.g., the acquired company’s Finance team) throughout the integration lifecycle.
  • Manage project execution across finance workstreams (e.g., tax, accounting, payroll, treasury) to support smooth and timely integration of financial operations, and flag risks and issues to senior team members and the cross-functional team for resolution.
  • Establish project management best practices across finance workstreams (e.g., tax, accounting, payroll, treasury) while identifying and raising key risks to the cross-functional team to ensure proactive resolution.
  • Support and execute the FP&A integration workstream for the acquired company, helping transition FP&A people, process, and technology and bring the P&L into Salesforce’s corporate process.
  • Provide timely communication to the leadership team of the acquired business and Salesforce executives on financial performance and key integration updates.
  • Refine and execute on the M&A integration playbook, ensuring the financial management and processes of the acquired business are fully integrated into Salesforce’s core teams.



Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting or a related quantitative field.
  • At least 5+ years of experience in finance, M&A integration, consulting, project management, or finance transformation projects.
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills with the ability to structure complex problems, develop hypotheses, and present data-driven solutions.

descriptionHtml:

About the team

We are looking for a technically strong Security Governance professional who can bridge the gap between Security & Compliance requirements and Engineering implementation.


This role will serve as the technical voice and face of Assurance. You will partner closely with Engineering organizations, PCLs, Product Security, Legal, and other stakeholders to understand how security and compliance requirements are implemented in real systems. You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.


The successful candidate will understand systems and architectures well enough to move beyond validating whether a control exists. They will evaluate how the control is designed, implemented, operated, and scaled across the enterprise.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Support Assurance and Engineering Alignment - Support technical liaison activities between Assurance, Engineering, Product Security, PCLs, and Legal, ensuring governance requirements are clearly understood and actionable.
  • Evaluate Control Implementation - Work directly with Engineering teams to understand how security and compliance controls are implemented within applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud environments, and engineering workflows.
  • Create the Engineering Feedback Loop - Assess what is working, what is creating unnecessary friction, and where controls or requirements are unclear or difficult to operationalize. Feed those insights back into control design, standards, and governance processes.
  • Make Requirements Engineer-Usable - Translate regulatory, compliance, and security expectations into clear, actionable technical requirements that Engineering teams can consistently implement and validate.
  • Develop Second-Line Oversight - Execute second-line oversight protocols that independently monitor, audit, and validate that all security controls are operational across engineering teams in Salesforce (e.g., attestations, CRE checks).
  • Understand Systems End-to-End - Develop a deep understanding of key platforms, architectures, engineering processes, security capabilities, and control implementations to help Assurance make better risk and compliance decisions.
  • Assess Risk in M&A - Assess control and risk exposure during M&As. Design the assessment to price risk, evaluate compatibility, and deliver an executable activation plan tied back to the risk model.
  • Partner on Emerging Security Requirements - Collaborate with Product Security, Legal, PCEs, Market Enablement, and other teams to understand emerging requirements and determine how they should translate into future security controls and engineering expectations.
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.
  • Support Enablement and Change Management - Contribute to change management efforts, documentation, and training to help engineering teams understand and comply with relevant policies and standards.
  • Support Control Incident Response - Participate in control incident reviews and postmortems, assisting with root-cause analysis and tracking remediation efforts for control failures.
  • Contribute to Control Refinement - Collaborate with control owners to provide feedback on control effectiveness and suggest updates based on operational findings and engineering feedback.
  • Engage Security Champions - Work alongside security and control champions across Engineering to gather feedback, distribute guidance, and support governance adoption.
  • Support Leadership Reporting - Help track and report metrics on control coverage, compliance trends, and risk items to support management reporting.
  • Represent Assurance Requirements - Serve as a point of contact for Assurance in engineering and operational discussions, helping integrate compliance considerations early in development cycles.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required. We're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 2-3 years of relevant experience or technical background in security engineering, cloud security, product security, IAM, platform engineering, or IT governance.
  • Ability to understand complex systems, architectures, APIs, infrastructure, cloud environments, and software development processes.
  • Experience translating security, risk, regulatory, or compliance requirements into technical implementation requirements.
  • Strong understanding of security controls and frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, SOC, SOX, FedRAMP, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with emerging technology and regulatory areas such as AI security, AI governance, privacy, and evolving global technology regulations.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering while also partnering with Legal, Compliance, Security, Risk, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical implementation details to governance teams and translate governance expectations into language Engineering teams can act on.
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to evaluate requirements and provide constructive input based on practical constraints.
  • Experience with independent control testing, assurance or audit practices, incident or root-cause analysis, or M&A due diligence is a plus.

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means creating a strong connection between what Assurance requires and what Engineering can effectively implement. Controls become more technically relevant, and requirements become easier for Engineering teams to consume. Implementation challenges are identified earlier, and emerging security and regulatory expectations are incorporated into the control environment before they become compliance gaps. Control failures are handled with the same rigor as availability incidents, and leadership has clear visibility into control reliability and systemic risk.


Ultimately, this role will help move Assurance from primarily validating compliance to becoming a technical governance partner that actively shapes secure and compliant engineering practices by design.

Partnering with Account Executives and Solution Engineers, you’ll support deals from first discovery call to storytelling demos and hands-on workshops, while growing your skills across Data 360, Agentforce and the wider Salesforce platform.


New to the title? A Solution Engineer (sometimes called a Pre-Sales Engineer or Sales Consultant) gathers business requirements, shapes the technical sales strategy, and demonstrates solutions that deliver business value, building customer confidence and clearing technical objections along the way. Increasingly, SEs also help customers adopt and get full value from what they’ve bought.


Core Responsibilities & Scope

Win Analytics business with Sales: Partner with Account Executives to understand each customer’s goals, manage several engagements at once across ANZ, and build trusted relationships with business leaders, analysts, data architects and data engineers.


Lead discovery and demos: Run discovery sessions and workshops, then build prototypes and customised demos that prove business value. Show how customers can define metrics and business rules once and reuse them everywhere, and how Tableau Semantics, Tableau Knowledge and Tableau Next (with Data 360 and Agentforce) fit their data stack.


Showcase AI and design AI-ready architectures: Demo Tableau Agent and natural-language analytics in Tableau Studio, and show how Tableau MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects trusted data to assistants such as Slack, Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot. Build generative AI and governed semantics into every customer architecture from the start.


Support bids, enable the team and represent Tableau: Contribute technical responses to RFPs, RFIs and RFTs, share knowledge with Solution Engineering and adjacent teams, feed customer insights back to Product, and represent Tableau at customer events and Tableau User Groups.


Minimum Requirements

  • Experience: 3+ years in technical pre-sales, consulting, customer success, analytics or data roles, plus a relevant degree (Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems or similar)
  • BI and data expertise: Hands-on experience with Tableau, CRM Analytics or similar tools (Power BI, Looker), plus familiarity with data modelling, semantic layers, and how data moves from warehouses, lakes and lakehouses through ETL/ELT pipelines into analytics-ready models.
  • AI fluency: Working knowledge of generative AI, including LLMs, prompt design, RAG and AI agents, and how they apply to analytics. You understand how MCP servers connect AI assistants to enterprise data and tools.
  • Communication and sales instinct: You present with confidence, in person and online, to audiences from analysts to executives. You can explain business value, position products, handle technical objections, and manage multiple sales cycles in parallel.

How you stand out

  • Experience with other cloud data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery), data prep tools (Informatica or similar), or semantic and metrics layers (Tableau Semantics, Published Data Sources, dbt)
  • Experience with Data 360 or Agentforce, or with setting up MCP servers to connect AI assistants to enterprise data
  • Salesforce certifications (Tableau Consultant, Tableau Desktop Specialist, CRM Analytics, Administrator), or Salesforce power-user or admin experience
  • A track record of building demos or proofs of concept, plus published content or community involvement such as blogs, talks or Tableau User Group activity

Expérience et compétences requises :

  • Expertise Commerciale : Plus de 3 ans d'expérience réussie dans la vente de logiciels ou de technologies avec des objectifs chiffrés (quota-carrying).

title: Real Estate Strategy and Planning Senior Manager
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Real Estate & Facility Management

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What You’ll Be Doing & Why It Matters

The Real Estate Strategy and Planning team shapes how Salesforce’s global office portfolio evolves. As Real Estate Strategy Senior Manager, you will be the finance lead behind our portfolio strategy and the key link between Real Estate, Finance and Transactions. You’ll turn real estate options into clear financial decisions by building scenario models, evaluating P&L impact and calculating return on investment. You’ll partner closely with Finance on long-range planning, budget, outlook and accounting impact, and with the Transactions team to turn the best scenarios into executed deals. Working with the VP of Real Estate Strategy and Planning and Finance, you’ll maintain a comprehensive long-range plan for the portfolio. Using AI tools and platforms, you’ll speed up modeling, analysis and reporting so leaders get answers faster.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Finance partnership: Serve as the main Real Estate partner to FP&A, Controllership and Accounting. Align on assumptions, budget and quarterly outlook, and make sure real estate impacts flow accurately into company plans and forecasts.
  • Transactions partnership: Work side by side with the Transactions team from scenario to signed deal. Model deal terms (rent, tenant improvement allowances, free rent, term, options), test proposals against the business case, and support negotiations with clear financial guidance.
  • Long-range planning: Partner with the VP of Real Estate Strategy and Planning and Finance to build and maintain a comprehensive long-range plan for the global portfolio, covering footprint, cost, capital and lease events. Keep it current as business plans change.
  • Scenario modeling: Build and own financial models for portfolio scenarios, including consolidations, expansions, exits, relocations, renewals vs. new deals, and footprint optimization.
  • Financial impact analysis: Quantify P&L, cash flow, capex/opex and balance sheet impact. Calculate ROI, NPV, IRR and payback to compare options and recommend a path.
  • Lease economics and accounting: Apply lease accounting knowledge, working with Accounting, so scenario outputs reflect the reported impact of decisions such as exits, renewals and early terminations.
  • Scorecard and metrics: Develop the REWS portfolio scorecard and metrics with Finance (cost per seat, cost per sq ft, utilization, occupancy, spend vs. plan). Monitor results and lead root cause analysis when metrics move.
  • Strategic initiatives: Lead the prioritization and delivery of high-visibility initiatives end to end, with full accountability for outcomes.
  • AI-enabled finance: Use AI tools and platforms to build and stress-test scenario models faster, automate recurring reporting and lease data analysis, and draft executive summaries and presentation materials. Find workflows that can be streamlined with AI or automation, and help the team adopt them.
  • Dashboards and interactive tools: Build dashboards and interactive scenario tools that let leaders explore financial tradeoffs and portfolio metrics on their own.
  • Executive communication: Write and edit complex analyses, decks and recommendations for senior leadership, and represent REWS with internal and external stakeholders.



Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in corporate finance, FP&A, real estate finance, investment banking or consulting
  • Expert financial modeling skills, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, DCF, ROI, NPV and IRR
  • Experience building and maintaining long-range plans or multi-year forecasts
  • Strong working knowledge of lease economics and lease accounting, and how real estate decisions flow through the P&L and balance sheet
  • Proven track record of partnering closely with Finance teams and deal or transaction teams to deliver results
  • Hands-on use of AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis and reporting, and to reduce manual work
  • Experience building business cases and recommendations for senior executives
  • Ability to lead cross-functional work and influence stakeholders across Finance, Accounting, Transactions and operating teams
  • Ability to think strategically while staying hands-on and detailed in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or related field



Preferred Qualifications

  • Corporate real estate experience, ideally with a multi-country or global office portfolio
  • Experience supporting real estate transactions, such as lease negotiations, renewals, exits or dispositions
  • Experience building KPI frameworks, dashboards and interactive tools in BI and AI platforms such as Tableau
  • Experience building AI-powered or automated finance workflows
  • MBA, CPA or CFA



About Real Estate and Workplace Services
The Real Estate and Workplace Services (REWS) organization designs, operates, and evolves the environments and experiences that enable Salesforce employees and customers to do their best work. Spanning more than 30 countries, our Agentic Campus reflects our values and culture – bringing together humans, agents, and robots to create inclusive, purpose-driven spaces where people feel a true sense of belonging. About the team


Assurance at Salesforce is being rebuilt as an engineering discipline. Legacy GRC runs on spreadsheets, screenshots, and an annual scramble to prove controls worked months ago. We're replacing it with a model that is continuous, automated, and built into how Salesforce ships. Controls are code. Evidence comes from pipelines, not people chasing tickets.

  • Risk-informed, control managed. We monitor, validate, and improve the controls that stand against threats and failures.
  • Visibility and invention. We give Salesforce a clear, current view of its security posture, and we invest in the people who build it.
  • Always in front. Nothing waits for the next audit to surface.

You'll have real ownership, a real roadmap, and the chance to define what modern assurance looks like for the industry.


What you'll be doing:


As a Sr. Security Governance Engineer, you'll translate enterprise security policies, regulatory requirements, and risk expectations into measurable, technically actionable controls. You'll help build a governance framework where policies and standards are version-controlled, validated, and integrated into engineering workflows. Over time, you'll grow into a Security Control Family Owner for domains such as IAM, Cloud, Application Security, Cryptography, Data Protection, or Infrastructure Security. The focus is governance, control design, and policy ownership. It is not hands-on software development.

  • Policy and standards: Develop and maintain security policies, technical standards, and control requirements. Manage the policy lifecycle: versioning, approvals, exceptions, reviews, and change management. Keep them aligned with architecture, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations.
  • Governance-as-Code / Policy-as-Code: Define structured, machine-readable policy and control requirements. Work with engineering to turn them into guardrails and validation criteria, using tools like OPA/Rego or cloud-native policy frameworks. You won't necessarily own the implementation. Review implementations for alignment with policy intent.
  • Control framework: Maintain a common control framework with clear objectives, ownership, and validation criteria. Establish traceability from regulation to policy to control to implementation. Set expectations for preventive, detective, and compensating controls, and support continuous evaluation of control effectiveness.
  • Control family ownership: Act as the SME and point of contact for your assigned domains. Interpret regulations, assess gaps, exceptions, and emerging risks, and recommend improvements.
  • Collaboration: Work with Security Engineering, Product Security, Cloud Security, IAM, Compliance, Risk, Audit, Legal, and business teams. Bring a governance perspective to architecture and design discussions.

Expected Outcomes

  • Decision speed: Rules are obvious, decisions are fast, and outputs are predictable, with governance built into the engineering workflow.
  • Scalable governance: Policies and control requirements are clear, consistent, and technically actionable.
  • Governance-as-Code adoption: Requirements are version-controlled, traceable, and integrated into security practices.
  • Alignment and visibility: Written policies, technical guardrails, and implemented controls match. Regulations, risks, controls, and evidence are clearly linked.
  • Control family SMEs: Dedicated owners set policy direction and technical standards for each domain.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required — we're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 2+ years in information security governance, security engineering, technology risk, or related functions
  • Strong grasp of security policies, standards, control frameworks, and governance processes
  • Familiarity with NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or PCI DSS
  • Ability to turn regulatory and security requirements into measurable control objectives
  • Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP), IAM, application, infrastructure, and data security
  • Understanding of control design (preventive and detective), risk assessment, and exception management
  • Familiarity with modern development practices, cloud environments, and CI/CD
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Governance-as-Code or Policy-as-Code, and policy engines such as OPA/Rego or HashiCorp Sentinel
  • Familiarity with YAML, JSON, Git, infrastructure-as-code, and DevSecOps
  • Experience with GRC platforms, Common Controls Frameworks (CCF), and OSCAL
  • Exposure to security posture management, compliance validation, architecture reviews, or AI governance

How We Work:

  • Engineering-first. We use version control, code review, CI/CD, and backlogs. Assurance work ships like software.
  • Automate first. If it's done manually twice, it's a candidate for a build.
  • Signals, not surprises. Gaps become alerts and workflows, and control failures resolve through defined escalation paths.
  • Embedded partners. We work alongside T&P teams as peers, not gatekeepers, and solve problems with them, not at them.
  • Outcomes over activity. We measure risk reduced, effort saved, and audit friction removed.
  • Room to grow. Learn the engineering side if you come from GRC, or the risk side if you come from engineering. We support both paths.

What You’ll Be Doing & Why It Matters

We are building the autonomous “software factory” that powers Slack’s global engineering organization.

As a Principal Member of Technical Staff (PMTS) / Staff Software Engineer on the Agentic Operations team, you will set the technical direction and architecture for how Slack builds, registers, and safely operates autonomous agentic systems. You will lead cross-team initiatives to transform high-volume software engineering workflows—from multi-repo code generation to automated incident remediation—into dependable, supervised, and continuously improving agentic pipelines at enterprise scale.

The Agentic Operations team builds and operates the platforms and internal “software factories” that automate how Slack’s engineering organization develops, operates, and maintains its services. Our mission is to turn repetitive, high-volume engineering toil into reliable, supervised autonomous workflows so engineers can focus on architecture and judgment.

We design and operate the systems that power:

  • Autonomous Code Generation & Remediation: Agent-driven pipelines that open, review, test, and land changes at scale across large codebases.
  • Operational & Incident Automation: Agents that assist with real-time incident response, post-incident remediation, and routine production maintenance.
  • Continuous Evaluation, Guardrails & Safety: Deterministic evaluation harnesses, regression test suites, and observability platforms that make non-deterministic agentic systems trustworthy in production.
  • Durable Execution & State Management: Robust execution engines featuring state persistence, function-calling hooks, human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates, and automated rollback mechanisms.
  • Continuous Data Hygiene: Agentic loops that keep Slack’s service catalog and entity metadata current and verified.



Our systems build on Slack’s agentic development platform (Speck), our Compute Platform (EKS, EC2), and the Service catalog. We define the patterns, guardrails, and operational standards that engineering teams across Slack adopt to safely run their own autonomous agents.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Set Technical Strategy & Architecture: Architect Slack’s agentic operations platform, defining the standards for building, registering, and operating autonomous agents and software factories safely at scale.
  • Build End-to-End Autonomous Pipelines: Design autonomous pipelines (code generation, bug fixing, incident remediation) equipped with orchestration, tool integrations, and human-in-the-loop controls needed to run unattended but accountably.
  • Establish Production AI Rigor: Build evaluation suites, regression harnesses, guardrails, and observability frameworks that make non-deterministic agentic systems measurable, debuggable, and safe.
  • Define Ownership & Accountability Models: Establish how failures in autonomous systems are detected, attributed, and remediated, including on-call policies and operational guardrails.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Adoption: Partner with platform teams (Speck, Incident Management, Deploy Safety) and consuming engineering groups to integrate agentic workflows into daily developer routines.
  • Cost & Compute Governance: Advocate for cost-conscious, efficient model and compute utilization, balancing model intelligence and latency against token budgets and compute spend.
  • Raise the Engineering Bar: Mentor senior engineers, drive deep architectural reviews, and author clear system designs that establish reusable technical patterns across the organization.



Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ Years of Software Engineering Experience: Proven track record designing and delivering complex distributed systems at scale, with Staff/Principal-level technical judgment and organizational influence.
  • Production Agentic Systems Experience: Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM-powered agents and multi-agent systems, including orchestration, structured tool/function calling, retrieval (RAG), and context window engineering.
  • Production AI Rigor & Evals: Concrete experience making non-deterministic AI systems production-ready through deterministic evaluation suites, regression harnesses, guardrails, and LLM telemetry.
  • Strong Distributed Systems & Backend Foundations: High engineering rigor in writing clean, scalable, maintainable code. Experience operating backend and distributed systems with direct accountability for uptime, latency, and reliability.
  • Systems-Level Automation Mindset: Pragmatic approach to developer platforms and automation, comfortable operating with ambiguity and balancing rapid AI capability against production safety.
  • Experience building autonomous code-generation pipelines, automated refactoring systems, or “software factories” that open PRs and land changes across monolithic or multi-repo architectures.
  • Experience designing agent evaluation frameworks, prompt/context management layers, or LLM observability platforms used by other engineering teams.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep background in service orchestration, or automated incident remediation at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS, Kubernetes (EKS), and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) using reusable, maintainable abstractions.
  • Active contributions to open-source agentic frameworks, developer tools, or the broader AI developer ecosystem.

  • Health & Life Sciences (HLS) – Collaborates with healthcare providers, payers, life sciences, pharmaceutical, and medical device companies to support digital health initiatives, regulatory compliance, and improved patient/member outcomes through the Salesforce platform (Direct experience with Health Cloud and/or Life Sciences Cloud strongly preferred).
  • Technology Media Telecommunication (TMT) – Works with technology companies, telecommunications providers, media organizations, and high-tech firms to accelerate innovation, improve customer success outcomes, and drive platform adoption at scale (Direct experience with Media Cloud strongly preferred).

You will partner closely with global practice leaders, onshore engagement managers, and enterprise customers. You will design, lead, and deliver architectures that solve critical business challenges. Slack Enterprise Grid & Administration

  • Familiarity with user/channel mapping schemas, export/import APIs, data parity verification, and cutover runbooks.



DevOps & Engineering Standards

  • Solid understanding of CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, automated testing, and secure API integration standards.
  • Experience hosting Slack apps on Heroku, AWS, GCP, or Azure.

  • Total Experience: 10-15+ years in software engineering, technical consulting, or enterprise cloud solutions.

The Experience

Join a team of 10 within Salesforce AI Labs, bringing computer-use AI into production with the autonomy of a small startup and the reach of Salesforce. We’re building Systems Integration Agent, announced at Dreamforce, which learns how to operate enterprise applications and turns complex workflows into reusable, code-backed automation. Customers are already running workflows in production; now we’re making that success repeatable across more systems and use cases.


Making computer use dependable raises hard engineering questions. How does an agent know it succeeded? When should it reason, and when should it follow a deterministic path? How should it recover when an application changes or ask for help before making a consequential mistake?


You’ll help answer those questions in production. Our team works directly with customers, building alongside them and turning discoveries into reusable product capabilities. As a Principal Engineer, you’ll remain hands-on while shaping architecture across our agent and backend systems, owning critical capabilities from design through operation, and helping other engineers deliver them.


What You'll Actually Be Doing

Drive Agent Development & Architecture

  • Design and build systems that learn from demonstrations and combine AI reasoning with deterministic execution to complete workflows reliably.
  • Develop recovery and verification capabilities so agents can adapt to changes, confirm outcomes, and recognize when human intervention is needed.
  • Build backend services with robust workflow state management, failure handling, and secure access to customer environments.
  • Create evaluations and diagnostics that measure task success, expose regressions, and make failures understandable.

Build Directly With Customers

  • Work alongside customers to understand their workflows, prototype solutions, and validate results in their environments.
  • Investigate where automation succeeds or fails, then turn those findings into improvements to the core product.
  • Help customers move from their first successful workflow toward repeatable, increasingly self-service adoption.
  • Partner with forward-deployed engineers and product management to decide which customer needs should shape the roadmap.

Shape Technical Direction & Grow the Team

  • Lead architectural decisions across agent execution, backend services, and workflow state, aligning system boundaries and tradeoffs with other technical leads.
  • Evaluate model selection, tool use, and context management against reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Raise the engineering bar through hands-on implementation, design reviews, and mentoring; help engineers take on broader ownership and participate in hiring.

You're Our Person If...

  • You’ve led the architecture and delivery of complex backend systems through deployment, production failures, and subsequent improvements, with impact across multiple components or teams.
  • You have hands-on experience shipping and operating LLM-powered systems, and can explain how evaluations and production failures informed your design decisions.
  • You can reason through concurrency, persistent state, retries, and partial failures in systems that perform consequential actions.
  • You’re proficient in Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • You can turn an unclear customer problem into a bounded technical approach, test it with users, and lead it through production while creating capabilities other engineers can build on.
  • You want direct customer engagement to be part of your engineering work, including investigating problems and discussing technical tradeoffs.
  • You use AI development tools thoughtfully and take responsibility for the correctness, security, and maintainability of what you ship.

Even Better If…

  • Agent tool use, code generation, automated recovery, or evaluation frameworks.
  • Browser automation, workflow orchestration, or enterprise integrations.

This is a ring-fenced, white-glove role supporting our two largest global systems integrator partners. You will be the single point of contact for partner program requests.

You will bridge Partner Sales Managers (PSM), Partner Account Managers (PAM), Program Operations and the partners' own operational stakeholders.

The work is hands-on and partner-facing. It involves taking calls, resolving issues quickly, and turning what you hear into operational change. It is not a back-office analyst role.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Be the first point of contact for partner program requests from your designated partners, taking some of the load off the PAMs and leaders who currently field these directly.
  • Answer partner calls and Slack messages, understand the issue, explain it internally and drive resolution.
  • Act as an escalation point for the Operational Specialists who execute requests.
  • Work directly with the partners' operational stakeholders.
  • Work with the Partner Sales team and PAMs/PSMs covering both partners. Keep them aligned and make sure requests are submitted correctly.
  • Act as an "assistant PAM": go between operations and the field, and speak credibly to both sides.
  • Join regular cadence meetings with partner leadership and PAMs.
  • Guide partners and internal teams through the details of program execution:Onboarding new partners, including contracting for sub-entitiesWhen and where benefits are eligibleProvisioning demo environments on the right orgsLegal and contracting requirementsEligibility for funding
  • Manage and recommend approvals for exceptions to written program benefits.
  • Support referral fee processes and communicate with the partners about them.
  • Help internal sales teams use program funds correctly and get the best return, working with the relevant sales leaders.
  • Give the Programs team clear, actionable recommendations on the unique program needs of your dedicated partners.
  • Where programs are being designed for these partners, such as custom benefits or incentives, bring in what you hear on the ground.
  • Keep a current picture of what is in, out and prioritized as deals change daily. Support end-to-end orchestration across the Catalyst support model.



Minimum Requirements

  • 6 to 8 years of experience
  • Directly stakeholder-facing, internally and externally, and comfortable leading discussions with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Polished and senior enough to represent the company brand to partner leadership and deliver external enablement.
  • Strong working knowledge of partner programs and the sales business, enough to speak credibly to both Operations and PAMs/PSMs.
  • Comfortable on the phone and handling escalations. These partners insist on calls and escalate quickly.
  • Skilled at turning findings into clear recommendations.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

Slack is seeking a Staff Researcher to help us understand how AI agents are changing the way people work together—and what that means for the future of workplace collaboration.

In this role, you will investigate how people and teams adopt, collaborate with, and delegate work to AI agents. You will explore not only individual experiences with AI, but also how agents affect shared context, coordination, communication, trust, and accountability across teams. Your research will help identify where agents create meaningful value, where they introduce friction or risk, and how Slack can better support collaboration among people and agents.

As a Staff-level individual contributor, you will independently shape and execute a research agenda with a primary focus on Slack's Ecosystem, understanding how AI agents affect the future of workplace collaboration. You will pair foundational research on emerging work practices with practical evaluation of product experiences, translating evidence into clear recommendations that influence product strategy and development. You will also mentor researchers and strengthen how the team conducts and applies research.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Lead research scoping, prioritization, and roadmapping across multiple teams focused on AI agents and workplace collaboration, turning ambiguous questions into focused, actionable research programs.
  • Study real-world workflows to understand how people discover, adopt, delegate to, supervise, and collaborate with agents—and how those behaviors affect team coordination, shared understanding, trust, and accountability.
  • Design and conduct rigorous foundational and evaluative research using a range of qualitative and quantitative methods, balancing depth, speed, and the limits of what each approach can establish.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and other insights functions to connect customer evidence with product decisions and triangulate findings across studies, behavioral data, and customer feedback.
  • Build compelling narratives and reusable frameworks that synthesize multiple lines of inquiry, identify new product opportunities, and make the user and business consequences of decisions clear.
  • Influence senior stakeholders through practical, evidence-based recommendations; help teams distinguish emerging signals from assumptions and prioritize the most important uncertainties.
  • Mentor colleagues and collaborate with Research Operations to improve research practices, tools, documentation, and the team's ability to deliver high-quality work efficiently.



Minimum Requirements

  • 8+ years of user or product research experience, or equivalent demonstrated experience delivering research at comparable scope and impact. A track record of independently leading ambiguous research across multiple product teams is more important than tenure alone.
  • Expertise in multiple research approaches, with strong qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis skills and sound judgment about methodological trade-offs.
  • Demonstrated experience translating research into product strategy, roadmap priorities, or consequential product decisions in a fast-moving product organization.
  • Strong synthesis, storytelling, and communication skills, including experience partnering with senior stakeholders and creating frameworks that help teams understand and act on evidence.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and mentoring skills, along with working fluency in AI assistants and agents and curiosity about their effects on real workplace behavior. You do not need to be an ML engineer.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Research experience with AI assistants, agents, automation, or human–AI interaction, including questions of delegation, oversight, trust, explainability, or recovery from errors.
  • Experience studying workplace collaboration, enterprise SaaS, knowledge workers, or multi-person and organizational workflows.
  • Experience with longitudinal studies, diary studies, contextual inquiry, or field research that captures how emerging tools become part of everyday work.
  • Experience partnering with Data Science to connect observed behaviors and customer needs with usage data and product evaluation.
  • Experience researching enterprise adoption, administrator needs, governance, or adoption barriers for emerging technologies.



We welcome researchers with a range of professional and educational backgrounds. If you can demonstrate the scope, research judgment, and impact described here, we encourage you to apply even if your experience does not map neatly to every qualification.

Slack is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our Desktop team within the Architecture & Systems organization. While most frontend roles focus on building user-facing features, this role is dedicated to building the Desktop Framework — the architectural foundation that underpins the Slack desktop client across all platforms. The team is heavily involved within the Electron open source project, ensuring the continued success and sustainability of the Electron ecosystem on behalf of Slack.

We are looking for an engineer who has deep expertise within Google's Chromium project, who is eager to lead cross functional efforts to uphold Slack security, performance, and stability within the web and desktop client. This engineer should love to keep up to date with the evolving capabilities of browser and desktop based development, be excited about the opportunity to increase developer efficiency and iterate on desktop security and development best practices alongside the rest of the Desktop and Frontend teams, and look forward to opportunities to collaborate across companies to align interests on a unified Electron vision.

Our success depends on working closely with other teams at Slack and at other companies, so communication and collaboration skills are a must. This is an opportunity to work on a team of skilled and impactful engineers that directly affects how Slack's desktop client is built.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Strategic Leadership: You will lead cross functional initiatives across Electron and at Slack associated with increasing developer productivity, OS level stability, performance, or security alongside desktop and frontend stakeholders.
  • Technical Standards: You will be contributing to key architectural decisions to adapt our existing frontend and desktop infrastructure to support new product features.
  • Navigating Ambiguity: You will thrive in ambiguity, often identifying and offering solutions to problems, like framework migrations or rendering bottlenecks, that are not yet evident to the leaders who presented them.
  • System Health: You will maintain and improve the core systems that power the Slack desktop client and Electron framework, including Slack and Electron-based infrastructure and tooling
  • Mentorship & Culture: You will build a safe space for learning and serve as a skilled and trusted mentor to engineers across the organization, developing the ability to coach new leaders rather than just individual contributors.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: You will collaborate with teammates across engineering to identify, define, and solve strategically important initiatives, acting as a leader in communication to de-escalate conflicts and drive consensus.



Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience writing client-side code (React + Typescript) for modern web applications at scale.
  • Deep Chromium experience, or experience contributing to large scale open source projects.
  • Development at Scale: Experience working in a large-scale, shared codebase with hundreds of contributors, where you have successfully established patterns that allow other teams to contribute effectively without friction. Experience writing understandable, testable code with an eye towards maintainability and scalability.
  • Strategic Architecture: Expertise in building complex systems and tooling, with the ability to lead technical design that guides the best decisions across the team.
  • Business Alignment: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to tie technical infrastructure your work succinctly to company goals like performance, reliability and developer velocity. Routinely and facilitates dialogue between junior and senior members to surface blockers.
  • Technical Breadth: Experience working with performance profiling and debugging tools for web based desktop applications. Familiarity with desktop development, along with the ability to understand and explain technical trade-offs and complexities.
  • Self-Awareness: A commitment to proactively offering regular, constructive feedback and gracefully receiving it to improve yourself and the team culture.
  • Eagerness to learn, but similar excitement to teach.
  • Understanding that the perfect solution is informed by the people who will be building on your work, rather than being purely dependent on technical merits. Empathy is a feature.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience contributing to the engineering reputation externally (e.g., blog posts, speaking at conferences, open source contributions).
  • Experience developing on Windows and maintaining build infrastructure for Windows desktop applications.
  • Experience in fast-paced and dynamic product development environments.

Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the Team

The Data 360 & Visualization Platform Operations team keeps the platforms that run Salesforce's own business running. We operate Data 360, CRM Analytics, and Tableau, the data and analytics foundation for how Salesforce sells, serves, and makes decisions. We are Customer Zero: we run these products at enterprise scale first, and what we learn goes back to the product teams.

  • Keep it up. Monitoring, alerting, and frontline incident response that catch problems before customers do.
  • Make it stable. Root-cause analysis of recurring failures, plus closing security and compliance findings.
  • Run it well. Cataloging supported assets, tracking run costs, and keeping practices consistent.
  • Make it easy to get help. One clear way to ask for support, backed by automation and AI agents.
  • Be Customer Zero. Regular performance reviews, with the evidence fed to product and engineering.

What it's like to join at this level: You'll be a trusted operator on a team that is rebuilding how it works. You already know how to run production; here you'll take the hardest recurring problems, own them to root cause, and turn what you learn into runbooks, monitors, and automation the whole team uses. You'll manage escalations and support processes with guidance from senior leads, and you'll help the analysts around you get better.
Who thrives here: You're curious, you want to know why something happened, and you stay calm when something breaks. You can explain technical issues clearly to non-technical people, and you leave every system a little better documented and a little more automated than you found it.

What Are We Looking For?

As a Senior Systems Analyst, Data Foundations, you'll independently own production support and administration for Salesforce's enterprise data and analytics platforms, with a strong grasp of native platform functionality and best practices. You'll help the team respond faster and resolve issues sooner, and you'll keep an eye on how satisfied our customers and partners are. You'll manage escalations across teams and time zones, act as a frontline responder who swarms incidents and knows when to pull in reliability engineers, own root-cause analysis through to resolution, and design monitoring that gives early warning. You'll shape lightweight support processes and reference material, and mentor analysts. You are an individual contributor and a go-to expert for your platform area.

Responsibilities

Escalation Management & Incident Response

  • Own escalations on cases, intake, and investigations across teams and time zones: set priority, route to the right engineering, SRE, or vendor owner, drive them to closure, and keep stakeholders informed.
  • Run follow-the-sun handoffs so escalations keep moving between Mexico City, Dublin, and Hyderabad without losing context.
  • Track escalation trends (volume, repeat causes, time to engage, time to resolve), and bring them to leads and platform engineering to drive fixes.
  • Be the escalation point for Tier-2 analysts on complex cases and investigations.
  • Be a frontline responder in incidents: connect first, assess impact, and use judgment on when to pull in Site Reliability Engineers (SREs). Manage the case, intake, and stakeholder communication workstream alongside Incident Command. SREs own incident resolution.
  • Meet individual and team lifecycle SLAs: First Response Time (FRT), Next Response Time (NRT), and Average Resolution Time (ART), and case satisfaction (CSAT) targets while keeping backlog health. You are measured against the same targets as the team.
  • Help L7 refine the intake and investigation lifecycle SLAs: mentor Systems Analysts on hitting them, and raise challenges where targets, routing, or processes make them hard to meet.
  • Spot patterns in SLA misses and satisfaction feedback, and bring recommended fixes to the L7 and the team.

Problem Management & RCA Ownership

  • Own root-cause analysis and resolution for application bugs and recurring failures, and close RCAs with verified fixes.
  • Troubleshoot complex declarative and low-code issues, and recommend code-level fixes to engineering partners.
  • Prioritize technical debt against the backlog to improve stability, and recommend fixes.

Reliability & Observability

  • Design and implement proactive monitors, alerts, and automations for platform health.
  • Contribute to design reviews and operating-model improvements (for example Operational Readiness practices).
  • Use automation and AI to reduce manual work and move the team toward self-healing operations.

Platform Administration & Enhancement

  • Deliver complex declarative solutions (Flows, validation rules, permission models) and manage enhancement projects from inception through support transition.
  • Own complex access and role-hierarchy design, bulk data loads and migrations, and sandbox management.
  • Reliably handle standard administration so the team can focus on higher-value work.

Process Engineering, SOPs & Support Reference Manuals

  • Own process engineering for your platform area: templates, process design, capture, and lifecycle (create, review, update, retire) of lightweight SOPs and Support Reference Manuals (SRMs). This is process design, not technical writing.
  • Request SRM inputs from Platform Engineering and create or manage them as needed, so support teams have the reference material they need before launch.
  • Keep SOPs and SRMs current and findable, and use them to reduce repeat escalations.
  • Write knowledge articles and business process maps that let Tier-1/Tier-2 teams resolve issues without escalation.
  • Act as SME and point of contact for development and product partners.

Security, SOX & Compliance

  • Maintain compliance with security policies and change controls.
  • Support technology compliance activities, audit reporting, and SOX controls, and help close findings.
  • Follow the SDLC (Agile) and change, deployment, incident, and problem management processes.

Collaboration & Growth

  • Partner effectively with vendors, engineers, and business teams across time zones.
  • Mentor Systems Analysts and new joiners, and share knowledge through documentation and team forums.
  • Try new tools and practices, and bring ideas that improve how the team works.

Flexibility

  • On-call and travel as required, subject to local regulations. Other related duties as required.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, business, or equivalent experience.
  • 0-3 years of hands-on platform or systems support, administration, or implementation experience in an enterprise IT environment.
  • Strong knowledge of Salesforce native functionality and best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage escalations across teams and time zones, respond as a frontline responder in incidents (including knowing when to pull in reliability engineers), and own RCAs through resolution.
  • Experience with declarative tools (Flow, validation rules), data loading, and troubleshooting complex data and configuration issues.
  • Working knowledge of Service Management practices (incident, problem, change) and the SDLC.
  • Ability to design lightweight processes, SOPs, and reference manuals that others can run.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently in a distributed, global team.
  • Certifications (achieved): Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201), Advanced Administrator (ADM-211), and Platform App Builder. Platform Developer I achieved or actively pursuing.

Preferred

  • Certifications: Data 360, Tableau, or other specialist or consultant certifications.
  • Hands-on experience with Data 360, Agentforce, CRM Analytics, or Tableau.
  • Experience building monitors, alerts, or automation (observability tooling, Flow, scripting).
  • Intermediate coding (Apex, Python, SQL).
  • Experience in SOX-controlled environments.
  • Experience mentoring or informally leading peers.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

  • Deliver hands-on configuration, development, and deployment of Informatica MDM SaaS solutions within defined architectural frameworks, with a focus on business domains such as Customer, Product, and Supplier.

  • Configure and implement Informatica MDM SaaS products including Customer 360 (C360) and Reference 360 (R360), covering ingestion, match/merge, survivorship, and hierarchy management.

  • Support legacy-to-cloud migration efforts by executing migration tasks, validating data integrity, and troubleshooting technical issues within modernization programs.
  • Apply data quality rules and governance standards using Cloud Data Quality (CDQ), contributing to lineage, profiling, and metadata enrichment workstreams.
  • Build and configure API integrations, event-driven pipelines, and batch ETL processes connecting MDM with upstream/downstream systems.
  • Develop and tune match/merge rules, survivorship logic, and custom task workflows to support business validation and stewardship operations.
  • Collaborate with architects, project managers, and customer stakeholders to communicate technical progress, surface risks, and propose solutions to implementation challenges.
  • Contribute to technical documentation including design specs, configuration guides, and handover materials that meet delivery and customer quality standards.
  • Apply AI and generative AI tools to accelerate configuration tasks, code generation, and documentation as part of standard delivery practice.

You’re Our Person If…

  • Hands-on experience with Informatica MDM SaaS (C360, R360, or multidomain MDM) is required.
  • Exposure to data governance concepts, tools, and frameworks (CDGC, metadata management, data lineage) is strongly preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
  • Travel to client sites (average of 10%), but maybe higher or lower based on the client engagement.

Candidates with only advisory, or project management backgrounds without current platform hands-on experience are not the right fit for this position.

Salesforce is seeking a high-impact Capacity Planning Director to drive multi-million dollar, strategic infrastructure decisions that directly safeguard and power our global platform health. Capacity Planners scope, analyze, and forecast the massive infrastructure demand supporting our diverse product portfolio at global scale. In this executive-facing leadership role, you will work across functions, leveraging deep technical expertise and advanced forecasting to influence and inform executive decision-making.


This leader will work closely with senior product owners, engineering leads, and technical service teams across Salesforce. You will synthesize disparate data streams to establish custom models, directly shaping multi-million dollar capital allocation and infrastructure investments. Partnering with top-level executive leadership, you will evaluate architectural frameworks, product and design roadmaps, go-to-market strategies, and user growth models to ensure long-term capacity health and operational efficiency.


In this role, you will manage both financial and availability risk across software and hardware. You will need the ability to dive deep technically with relevant engineering teams and ask probing questions. It is also critical that you can context switch and operate both at the tactical, short-term execution level and the longer term, multi-year, strategic level. Deep strategic knowledge of public cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) and multi-substrate architectural boundaries is essential to drive high-stakes trade-offs and portfolio-wide resource planning. 


The role requires comfort with data-driven storytelling, strategic acumen, and the ability to build trust at the highest organizational levels. As a steward of Salesforce’s long-term infrastructure investment strategy, your vision and leadership will influence critical multi-million dollar business outcomes.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Enhance a trusted capacity planning data foundation that reconciles service demand, infrastructure utilization, cloud reservations, supplier availability, and cost, with clear metric definitions, ownership, and automated quality checks.
  • Lead the development and validation of demand forecasts and scenario models that quantify uncertainty, capacity shortfall risk, and the cost of excess capacity. Track forecast accuracy and bias, and use actual results to improve planning assumptions.
  • Manage a team of 3-5 capacity planners who manage reservations for various subsets of service owners across multiple IaaS providers.
  • Establish a trusted capacity planning data foundation that reconciles service demand, infrastructure utilization, cloud reservations, supplier availability, and cost, with clear metric definitions, ownership, and automated quality checks.
  • Lead the development and validation of demand forecasts and scenario models that quantify uncertainty, capacity shortfall risk, and the cost of excess capacity. Track forecast accuracy and bias, and use actual results to improve planning assumptions.

  • Develop the team’s SQL, Python, statistical modeling, and AI capabilities through coaching, reusable analytical methods, and peer review.
  • Apply AI assistants and agent workflows to automate data investigation, variance analysis, scenario preparation, and executive reporting. Measure improvements in planning cycle time and analytical quality, with human review of consequential recommendations.
  • Develop the team’s SQL, Python, statistical modeling, and AI capabilities through coaching, reusable analytical methods, and peer review.

Minimum Requirements

  • Candidate should have 7+ years of experience in operations, business intelligence, strategy, capacity planning, financial modeling, analytics or similar positions in a related field
  • Strong analytical skills with experience consolidating complex datasets across various unconnected systems and platforms to tell a clear story. 
  • Fundamental knowledge of systems infrastructure and how services interact with the underlying hardware 
  • Experience building statistical models 
  • Proven track record using data to influence, advise, and align C-suite and board-level executives at large public companies on complex, high-stakes infrastructure and financial investments
  • Experience presenting data in a consistent and repeatable manager to various stakeholders
  • Attention to detail with a focus on data quality
  • BA/BS in Statistics, Economics, Business, Operations, or Computer Science/Engineering is preferred. Equivalent degree, or experience is equally acceptable.
  • Proficiency with SQL, Python, Claude skills/MCP and prompt engineering experience
  • Experience in capacity management, planning, forecasting and scheduling is a plus

Preferred Qualifications

Ability to explain model assumptions, distinguish forecast error from changes in business demand, and translate uncertainty into capacity and investment recommendations.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Applying strong prospecting skills to develop business within new and existing accounts
  • Defining and crafting account plans to map out business opportunities and build a healthy, scalable pipeline
  • Acting as a trusted advisor to your customers, developing strong relationships across stakeholders at all levels — from key influencers through to C-suite executives
  • Leading value-driven sales conversations that clearly communicate the impact and return on investment our solutions deliver
  • Managing your sales cycle effectively for longer, more complex engagements in Enterprise
  • Partnering with a virtual internal team to build strategic plans tailored to each account, bringing in the right people at the right time
  • Collaborating with your Salesforce counterparts to identify and close joint solution sales opportunities across your portfolio



Minimum Requirements

  • Experience: A proven track record of quota-carrying sales experience, successfully selling software or SaaS solutions across organisations of varying size and complexity. Experience managing both transactional and multi-year licence agreements is desirable. An understanding of the analytics and BI industry is a plus
  • Curiosity: You are inquisitive and always looking to learn and discover what your customers need; you keep track of market trends and are committed to continuously developing your own skills
  • Stakeholder confidence: You are able to build trust with any stakeholder, from end users and department heads to C-level executives, adapting your style to suit the audience and the deal
  • Results-driven: You are consistently motivated to meet and exceed your targets, as reflected in your track record of quota attainment across both new and existing business
  • Sales excellence: You have highly developed prospecting, planning, and closing skills — whether managing a high volume of deals or a focused set of strategic accounts
  • Initiative: You take initiative and are proactive in identifying and pursuing new opportunities, bringing energy and focus to both your pipeline and your customer relationships
  • Communication: Networking and relationship building come naturally to you. You know what to say, and when to say it
